Deduplicate only repeated accounting references to the same occurrence, kind, location and exact source-value hash. Never merge distinct supplied occurrences, even with identical hashes. Order and retained source identity determine stable accounting references; canonical record IDs still use §34.2. Count the entire resulting unit universe, including inventory, structural and inaccessible units, when applying the unchanged §6.5A limits. The raw-unit challenge condition is strictly greater than 500, not greater than or equal to 500; every other size-independent trigger remains effective.

Let P be the parent archive's C occurrence path, already bound to the owning input version. Number central-directory entries from zero in their exact central-directory order, not local-file-offset order, canonical-filename order or extraction completion order. The child occurrence for entry i is P followed by i. Different supplied archives and different nested occurrences remain distinct even when bytes or names are equal. Local/central identity validation is still required; choosing central-directory order for accounting does not weaken it.

Only fully verified members receive ACCESSIBLE ZIP_MEMBER values with observed expanded hashes/lengths. An exposed member means a central-directory record with the exact central signature and complete in-bounds fixed header, filename, extra area and comment area, within the established central-directory extent and traversal order. Its entry index and central-header offset establish the member locator even when local validation or expansion fails. Preserve each such exposed occurrence, including duplicate names, directories, links and unsupported entries, as INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED with value=null when it cannot be validated; do not expand it or grant its path authority. It still receives exactly one child ARTIFACT_INVENTORY at P followed by i under C: when verified expanded bytes are unavailable, both byteLength and contentSha256 are null, with an explicit blocked disposition. A claimed member size or digest does not fill these values. Distinct colliding/duplicate central occurrences are never merged to hide them. No child inventory is created for a guessed entry, unparsed count or incomplete/unbounded central record.

When a depth, entry, byte, ratio, path, name, worker or work bound actually stops a recognized child, retain that child's already exposed member occurrence, inventory and available exact bytes, mark its unresolved subdivision INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED with the precise cause, and stop the affected expansion safely. It is neither a successful opaque fallback nor proof that children do not exist. Never reset counters for nested ZIPs, invoke unbounded recursive decompression, fabricate descendants, or treat unknown remaining units as zero. A separately supplied copy is a separate root occurrence with its own identity and is charged again to the same input-version pass counters; equality of bytes does not merge it or reset the budget.

When a depth, entry, byte, ratio, path, name, worker or work bound actually stops a recognized child, retain that child's already exposed member occurrence, inventory and available exact bytes, mark its unresolved subdivision INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED with the precise cause, and stop the affected expansion safely. It is neither a successful opaque fallback nor proof that children do not exist. Never reset counters for nested ZIPs, invoke unbounded recursive decompression, fabricate descendants, or treat unknown remaining units as zero. A separately supplied copy is a separate root occurrence with its own identity and is charged again to the same input-version pass counters; equality of bytes does not merge it or reset the budget.

statement: Retain the decoder’s complete consistent local/central-header, boundary, safe noncolliding canonical-path, actual expanded-length, CRC/SHA-256, permitted-flag/extra and resource/platform checks; earlier bound stops, central-directory accounting order, and bounded metadata exposure never weaken those checks.

sourceLocations.text: The supported decoding subset is ordinary single-volume ZIP and the decoder's bounded ZIP64 forms, with stored or DEFLATE compression, permitted data descriptors, UTF-8 or CP437 names and the decoder's validated Unicode-path extras. Keep its existing checks for complete consistent local/central headers, exact boundaries, safe noncolliding canonical paths, actual expanded lengths, CRC and SHA-256, permitted flags/extras and resource/platform bounds. Encrypted entries, split volumes, self-extracting prefixes, directory/link/device/special entries, unsupported compression/extra fields and ambiguous or colliding paths do not become supported through this mapping. The exact intake safety profile below and existing worker isolation remain effective. The response transport contract remains unchanged. A resource or platform failure is not reclassified as an unsupported format to bypass a blocker. Intake uses this decoder's structural/byte validation, not the inbound response's manifest, response.json role or attachment-admission semantics.

Use a centralized, versioned intake profile closed-loop-raw-units-zip-limits/1. Its bounds are: 27 cumulative central-directory entries across the entire selected input-version archive-mapping pass, including every supplied root and recursively decoded child; 67108864 bytes per expanded member; 70254592 cumulative reserved-or-produced expanded bytes; 140509184 cumulative archive bytes submitted to decoding (count a nested archive again when it is submitted); compression ratio at most 1100 per member; filename byte length at most 65535; canonical path depth at most 128; maximum archive nesting level 27 with the supplied archive at level 1; and one cumulative elapsed-worker deadline of 600000 ms for that entire input-version archive-mapping pass. The entry budget is charged on exposure before expansion, including unsupported/blocked entries; the maximum depth cannot bypass that budget. Expansion and byte accounting are checked before allocation and incrementally, against both declared and actual lengths; declared metadata never substitutes for verified bytes. The expansion safety counter reserves each declared output length before allocation; actual production within that reservation does not charge the same byte twice, while any additional produced byte must first fit and consume remaining budget. Every produced/reserved byte remains charged even if later CRC, validation or decoding fails; no refund, reset or retry can escape the pass-wide ceiling. It includes every child occurrence at every depth, including a nested archive's bytes as its parent's output and its own children separately. This work-safety counter is distinct from the semantic aggregate-byte review sum, which includes only actually verified retained child bytes. The archive-byte sum counts each archive occurrence once when submitted to decoding. The same original per-archive structural and byte checks remain; a bound can stop processing earlier, never authorize weaker checking. These ceilings reuse the current default decoder's 27 entries, 64 MiB file bound, 64 MiB + 1 MiB response + 2 MiB manifest total, twice-total archive bound, ratio/name/path/work bounds; the intake profile assigns those generic ceilings without granting any response.json/manifest.json role or larger filename-specific allowance. Transport recursiveExpansion=false and maxNestingDepth=0 remain response-transport rules, not intake accounting rules. A lower already-applicable storage/worker bound still stops work and remains explicitly blocked; it must not silently change this profile or yield favorable completeness. The exact profile-hash preimage is C({"version":"closed-loop-raw-units-zip-limits/1","scope":"INPUT_VERSION_PASS","maxEntries":27,"maxEntryBytes":67108864,"maxExpandedBytes":70254592,"maxArchiveBytes":140509184,"maxCompressionRatio":1100,"maxFilenameBytes":65535,"maxPathDepth":128,"maxNestingDepth":27,"workerTimeoutMs":600000}); its SHA-256 is the profile hash. The retained unitization derivation binds the owning input version, mapping ID, this exact profile ID/hash, actual counters and completion/blocker status; changed profile or source invalidates reuse under the existing derivation rules. Repeated equal roots and members are charged separately. Any future profile change follows existing versioning and acceptance requirements.

Let P be the parent archive's C occurrence path, already bound to the owning input version. Number central-directory entries from zero in their exact central-directory order, not local-file-offset order, canonical-filename order or extraction completion order. The child occurrence for entry i is P followed by i. Different supplied archives and different nested occurrences remain distinct even when bytes or names are equal. Local/central identity validation is still required; choosing central-directory order for accounting does not weaken it.

Preserve independently established exact metadata and comment spans as their corresponding ACCESSIBLE structural units even when the owning member is blocked; accessibility here concerns the exact metadata bytes, not the member's safe expansion or semantic validity. An extra field receives its specified unit only when its own 4-byte header and full declared payload are in bounds; duplicate/unsupported fields can be preserved as separate observed bytes but still block member admission. If malformed metadata prevents complete field segmentation, preserve the exact whole extra-area bytes as diagnostic provenance on the blocked occurrence, without inventing extra-field units. For a blocked member whose local metadata is not safely established, emit only established central metadata/extras/comments, then its blocked child inventory. This is bounded read-only exposure; it does not relax existing decoder rejection. Unknown remaining structure remains an explicit archive-level blocker, and a smaller observed count cannot discharge it.

sourceLocations.text: The supported decoding subset is ordinary single-volume ZIP and the decoder's bounded ZIP64 forms, with stored or DEFLATE compression, permitted data descriptors, UTF-8 or CP437 names and the decoder's validated Unicode-path extras. Keep its existing checks for complete consistent local/central headers, exact boundaries, safe noncolliding canonical paths, actual expanded lengths, CRC and SHA-256, permitted flags/extras and resource/platform bounds. Encrypted entries, split volumes, self-extracting prefixes, directory/link/device/special entries, unsupported compression/extra fields and ambiguous or colliding paths do not become supported through this mapping. The exact intake safety profile below and existing worker isolation remain effective. The response transport contract remains unchanged. Use a centralized, versioned intake profile closed-loop-raw-units-zip-limits/1. Its bounds are: 27 cumulative central-directory entries across the entire selected input-version archive-mapping pass, including every supplied root and recursively decoded child; 67108864 bytes per expanded member; 70254592 cumulative reserved-or-produced expanded bytes; 140509184 cumulative archive bytes submitted to decoding (count a nested archive again when it is submitted); compression ratio at most 1100 per member; filename byte length at most 65535; canonical path depth at most 128; maximum archive nesting level 27 with the supplied archive at level 1; and one cumulative elapsed-worker deadline of 600000 ms for that entire input-version archive-mapping pass. The entry budget is charged on exposure before expansion, including unsupported/blocked entries; the maximum depth cannot bypass that budget. Expansion and byte accounting are checked before allocation and incrementally, against both declared and actual lengths; declared metadata never substitutes for verified bytes. The expansion safety counter reserves each declared output length before allocation; actual production within that reservation does not charge the same byte twice, while any additional produced byte must first fit and consume remaining budget. Every produced/reserved byte remains charged even if later CRC, validation or decoding fails; no refund, reset or retry can escape the pass-wide ceiling. It includes every child occurrence at every depth, including a nested archive's bytes as its parent's output and its own children separately. This work-safety counter is distinct from the semantic aggregate-byte review sum, which includes only actually verified retained child bytes. The archive-byte sum counts each archive occurrence once when submitted to decoding. The same original per-archive structural and byte checks remain; a bound can stop processing earlier, never authorize weaker checking. These ceilings reuse the current default decoder's 27 entries, 64 MiB file bound, 64 MiB + 1 MiB response + 2 MiB manifest total, twice-total archive bound, ratio/name/path/work bounds; the intake profile assigns those generic ceilings without granting any response.json/manifest.json role or larger filename-specific allowance. Transport recursiveExpansion=false and maxNestingDepth=0 remain response-transport rules, not intake accounting rules. A lower already-applicable storage/worker bound still stops work and remains explicitly blocked; it must not silently change this profile or yield favorable completeness. The exact profile-hash preimage is C({"version":"closed-loop-raw-units-zip-limits/1","scope":"INPUT_VERSION_PASS","maxEntries":27,"maxEntryBytes":67108864,"maxExpandedBytes":70254592,"maxArchiveBytes":140509184,"maxCompressionRatio":1100,"maxFilenameBytes":65535,"maxPathDepth":128,"maxNestingDepth":27,"workerTimeoutMs":600000}); its SHA-256 is the profile hash. The retained unitization derivation binds the owning input version, mapping ID, this exact profile ID/hash, actual counters and completion/blocker status; changed profile or source invalidates reuse under the existing derivation rules. Repeated equal roots and members are charged separately. Any future profile change follows existing versioning and acceptance requirements.

statement: Apply the same byte/claim ZIP-recognition test to every supplied root and every verified expanded child.

sourceLocations.text: Apply the same recognition test to each supplied root and each verified expanded child. A byte candidate exists if the first four bytes are a ZIP local-header, EOCD, ZIP64 EOCD or ZIP64-locator signature (respectively hexadecimal 504b0304, 504b0506, 504b0606, 504b0607), or if the EOCD signature 504b0506 occurs anywhere in the last min(byteLength,65557) bytes. Also attempt validation when a supplied filename ends with .zip under ASCII case-insensitive comparison, or the supplied media type, before a semicolon and after ASCII whitespace trim/case-fold, is application/zip or application/x-zip-compressed. Names and media types can require an attempt but cannot suppress a byte candidate or establish success. A random signature or claimed filename can never create successful ZIP coverage: the complete retained structural, boundary, path and integrity checks decide that. Missing bytes retain an unavailable inventory/blocker; they do not establish absence of ZIP structure. Noncandidate bytes without a ZIP claim do not receive ZIP nodes through speculation; C's other available accounting rules remain applicable.

For every verified expanded child, apply the byte/claim recognition test above. A ZIP candidate is mapped recursively by this same mapping, in depth-first central-directory order, under the entire input-version mapping pass's shared cumulative safety counters and deadline. The expanded child becomes the next archive occurrence P; no new root identity, fresh budget or favorable parent result is substituted. Exact expanded bytes remain retained and bound even when their own ZIP structure is blocked. A ZIP-based document can expose these ZIP members without thereby claiming semantic Office/XML/PDF parsing. A child that is not a ZIP candidate still receives its inventory and applicable exact UTF-8 physical spans under C; this addendum invents no other media mapping.

Existing duplicate/unsupported/malformed-extra rejection is unchanged. No decoded timestamp, UID, Unicode name or other extra interpretation replaces its exact source bytes.

4. ZIP_MEMBER_COMMENT only when the central entry's comment length is nonzero. locatorValue is ["MEMBER_COMMENT", i, offset]. v has exactly offset, byteLength and rawHex. Empty comments create no comment unit. These bytes are counted even though comments have no transport authority.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText:
No other stage-operation combination is valid. The registry declares for each listed operation its allowed response types, target-slot derivation, required input families, writable fields and collections, reservation requirement, independence requirement, completion predicate, retry behavior, and whether it is agent, human, or application executed.

Operation execution and response permissions are closed:

- External-agent operations are COMPLETE at Stages 01-09, 15, 21, 23, 24, 25, and 26; SEMANTIC_CHALLENGE; RECONCILE_INTAKE; SEARCH_ADEQUACY_REVIEW; RECONCILE_SOURCE_SEARCH; RECONCILE_RESEARCH; DISPOSITION_CHALLENGE; ATOMICITY_CHALLENGE; RECONCILE_REQUIREMENTS; SEMANTIC_REVIEW; RECONCILE_REQUIREMENT_SET; PROOF_REVIEW; RECONCILE_VERIFICATION_SUITE; EXECUTE_RUN; VERIFY; COMPARE; ROOT_CAUSE; REGRESSION; CORRECT; RECONCILE at Stage 26; ADVISORY_REVIEW at Stage 27; EXECUTE_EXTERNAL_TEST; INVESTIGATE_MISSING_EVIDENCE; and EXECUTE_FAILURE_TEST, EXECUTE_REGRESSION, and REGRESSION_VERIFY when externally routed. They require an operation reservation and file-first package. Their responseType is exactly DATA_PROPOSAL, HUMAN_INPUT_REQUIRED, BLOCKED, or EXECUTION_FAILED as permitted by the operation's field contract. ADVISORY_REVIEW at Stage 27 is optional and non-gating: it writes releaseGateReviews records only and cannot modify, delay, or substitute for any CALCULATE_RELEASE input, calculation, or state.
- Application commands are EXECUTE_FAILURE_TEST when natively routed, EXECUTE_REGRESSION when natively routed, REGRESSION_VERIFY when natively routed, FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, COMPLETE at Stage 18, CONFIRM at Stage 19, FREEZE_BASELINE, RUN_NATIVE_TESTS, RUN_NATIVE_ATTACKS, FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE, VERIFY_IDENTITY, CALCULATE_RELEASE, CALCULATE_EVIDENCE_CHAINS, and CALCULATE_TERMINAL. They accept no external response envelope and commit only application-owned results through the universal command path. COMPLETE at Stage 18 and CONFIRM at Stage 19 are application-calculated convergence and confirmation determinations; agents contribute only the separately declared explanatory fields of the owning record families. FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, FREEZE_BASELINE, and FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE consume and reference the required current humanDecisions records; they never create human authority.
- HUMAN_DECISION commands are CAPTURE_DELIVERY_INTENT; application confirmation of a newly reported human-origin answer; and RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION, one global application-validated command bound to exactly one registered purpose and target per invocation. The closed RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION purpose enum is INTENT_CONFIRMATION, CANDIDATE_COMPONENT_SELECTION, BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, DISCLOSURE_AUTHORIZATION, EXTERNAL_ACTION_RISK_AUTHORIZATION, CONTROLLED_EXCEPTION, REGRESSION_RETIREMENT_AUTHORIZATION, BACKUP_POLICY_SELECTION, TRADEOFF_OR_SCOPE_DECISION, VISUAL_BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, and HUMAN_AUTHORITY_CORRECTION. Each purpose writes only the humanDecisions record and the human-decision-owned fields FIELD_REGISTRY declares for that purpose and target. HUMAN commands are SAVE_HUMAN_INPUT, which creates and edits User Job Input and saves Section 18 fallback answers with their declared consequences, and RECORD_HUMAN_OBSERVATION, which records human-owned observation and evidence records for human-inspection routes. These commands write only their declared HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION fields and records, accept no agent-owned canonical fields, and accept no external response envelope.
- EXPORT_PROMPT_FILE, EXPORT_EXECUTION_PACKAGE, SELECT_RESPONSE_JSON_FILE, SELECT_RETURNED_FILES, EXPORT_OR_SHARE_AUTHORIZED_ARTIFACTS, and RECORD_DELIVERY_EVIDENCE are operator actions. They create only the application receipts and human or external evidence explicitly declared by their contracts.

For every operation, TARGET_SLOT = SHA-256(closed-loop-canonical-json/1 of contractProfileId, jobId, stage, operation, and all operation-specific target identities required by Section 14.7). The target slot excludes projectRevision so an exact retry retains its slot; expectedRevision and scopeHash remain separate mandatory preconditions. No operation can write a family or field not listed in its FIELD_REGISTRY entry.

No other stage-operation combination is valid. The registry declares for each listed operation its allowed response types, target-slot derivation, required input families, writable fields and collections, reservation requirement, independence requirement, completion predicate, retry behavior, and whether it is agent, human, or application executed.

Operation execution and response permissions are closed:

- External-agent operations are COMPLETE at Stages 01-09, 15, 21, 23, 24, 25, and 26; SEMANTIC_CHALLENGE; RECONCILE_INTAKE; SEARCH_ADEQUACY_REVIEW; RECONCILE_SOURCE_SEARCH; RECONCILE_RESEARCH; DISPOSITION_CHALLENGE; ATOMICITY_CHALLENGE; RECONCILE_REQUIREMENTS; SEMANTIC_REVIEW; RECONCILE_REQUIREMENT_SET; PROOF_REVIEW; RECONCILE_VERIFICATION_SUITE; EXECUTE_RUN; VERIFY; COMPARE; ROOT_CAUSE; REGRESSION; CORRECT; RECONCILE at Stage 26; ADVISORY_REVIEW at Stage 27; EXECUTE_EXTERNAL_TEST; INVESTIGATE_MISSING_EVIDENCE; and EXECUTE_FAILURE_TEST, EXECUTE_REGRESSION, and REGRESSION_VERIFY when externally routed. They require an operation reservation and file-first package. Their responseType is exactly DATA_PROPOSAL, HUMAN_INPUT_REQUIRED, BLOCKED, or EXECUTION_FAILED as permitted by the operation's field contract. ADVISORY_REVIEW at Stage 27 is optional and non-gating: it writes releaseGateReviews records only and cannot modify, delay, or substitute for any CALCULATE_RELEASE input, calculation, or state.
- Application commands are EXECUTE_FAILURE_TEST when natively routed, EXECUTE_REGRESSION when natively routed, REGRESSION_VERIFY when natively routed, FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, COMPLETE at Stage 18, CONFIRM at Stage 19, FREEZE_BASELINE, RUN_NATIVE_TESTS, RUN_NATIVE_ATTACKS, FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE, VERIFY_IDENTITY, CALCULATE_RELEASE, CALCULATE_EVIDENCE_CHAINS, and CALCULATE_TERMINAL. They accept no external response envelope and commit only application-owned results through the universal command path. COMPLETE at Stage 18 and CONFIRM at Stage 19 are application-calculated convergence and confirmation determinations; agents contribute only the separately declared explanatory fields of the owning record families. FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, FREEZE_BASELINE, and FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE consume and reference the required current humanDecisions records; they never create human authority.
- HUMAN_DECISION commands are CAPTURE_DELIVERY_INTENT; application confirmation of a newly reported human-origin answer; and RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION, one global application-validated command bound to exactly one registered purpose and target per invocation. The closed RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION purpose enum is INTENT_CONFIRMATION, CANDIDATE_COMPONENT_SELECTION, BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, DISCLOSURE_AUTHORIZATION, EXTERNAL_ACTION_RISK_AUTHORIZATION, CONTROLLED_EXCEPTION, REGRESSION_RETIREMENT_AUTHORIZATION, BACKUP_POLICY_SELECTION, TRADEOFF_OR_SCOPE_DECISION, VISUAL_BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, and HUMAN_AUTHORITY_CORRECTION. Each purpose writes only the humanDecisions record and the human-decision-owned fields FIELD_REGISTRY declares for that purpose and target. HUMAN commands are SAVE_HUMAN_INPUT, which creates and edits User Job Input and saves Section 18 fallback answers with their declared consequences, and RECORD_HUMAN_OBSERVATION, which records human-owned observation and evidence records for human-inspection routes. These commands write only their declared HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION fields and records, accept no agent-owned canonical fields, and accept no external response envelope.
- EXPORT_PROMPT_FILE, EXPORT_EXECUTION_PACKAGE, SELECT_RESPONSE_JSON_FILE, SELECT_RETURNED_FILES, EXPORT_OR_SHARE_AUTHORIZED_ARTIFACTS, and RECORD_DELIVERY_EVIDENCE are operator actions. They create only the application receipts and human or external evidence explicitly declared by their contracts.

For every operation, TARGET_SLOT = SHA-256(closed-loop-canonical-json/1 of contractProfileId, jobId, stage, operation, and all operation-specific target identities required by Section 14.7). The target slot excludes projectRevision so an exact retry retains its slot; expectedRevision and scopeHash remain separate mandatory preconditions. No operation can write a family or field not listed in its FIELD_REGISTRY entry.

18. Human clarification

The human interacts conversationally.
The human MUST NOT be required to construct final-machine JSON during clarification.

For every stage:
- the agent may ask genuinely human-only questions conversationally;
- the agent must not ask for available facts again;
- the agent must not ask for facts reliably obtainable from authorized materials or research;
- later-discovered human-only decisions are asked at the stage where they become necessary;
- one strict final JSON response file is returned only when the stage is ready.

humanInputRequests is the final structured fallback, not the normal conversation format.

They require an operation reservation and file-first package. Their responseType is exactly DATA_PROPOSAL, HUMAN_INPUT_REQUIRED, BLOCKED, or EXECUTION_FAILED as permitted by the operation's field contract. ADVISORY_REVIEW at Stage 27 is optional and non-gating: it writes releaseGateReviews records only and cannot modify, delay, or substitute for any CALCULATE_RELEASE input, calculation, or state.
- Application commands are EXECUTE_FAILURE_TEST when natively routed, EXECUTE_REGRESSION when natively routed, REGRESSION_VERIFY when natively routed, FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, COMPLETE at Stage 18, CONFIRM at Stage 19, FREEZE_BASELINE, RUN_NATIVE_TESTS, RUN_NATIVE_ATTACKS, FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE, VERIFY_IDENTITY, CALCULATE_RELEASE, CALCULATE_EVIDENCE_CHAINS, and CALCULATE_TERMINAL. They accept no external response envelope and commit only application-owned results through the universal command path. COMPLETE at Stage 18 and CONFIRM at Stage 19 are application-calculated convergence and confirmation determinations; agents contribute only the separately declared explanatory fields of the owning record families. FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, FREEZE_BASELINE, and FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE consume and reference the required current humanDecisions records; they never create human authority.
- HUMAN_DECISION commands are CAPTURE_DELIVERY_INTENT; application confirmation of a newly reported human-origin answer; and RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION, one global application-validated command bound to exactly one registered purpose and target per invocation. The closed RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION purpose enum is INTENT_CONFIRMATION, CANDIDATE_COMPONENT_SELECTION, BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, DISCLOSURE_AUTHORIZATION, EXTERNAL_ACTION_RISK_AUTHORIZATION, CONTROLLED_EXCEPTION, REGRESSION_RETIREMENT_AUTHORIZATION, BACKUP_POLICY_SELECTION, TRADEOFF_OR_SCOPE_DECISION, VISUAL_BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, and HUMAN_AUTHORITY_CORRECTION. Each purpose writes only the humanDecisions record and the human-decision-owned fields FIELD_REGISTRY declares for that purpose and target. HUMAN commands are SAVE_HUMAN_INPUT, which creates and edits User Job Input and saves Section 18 fallback answers with their declared consequences, and RECORD_HUMAN_OBSERVATION, which records human-owned observation and evidence records for human-inspection routes. 17.11 Date and time contract

All machine date-time values use RFC 3339 strings. Instants use UTC with uppercase Z and exactly three fractional-second digits. Date-only values use YYYY-MM-DD and are never coerced to an instant. Leap-second values are rejected. Offset-bearing input may be accepted only at an external boundary and is normalized to UTC while preserving the original value as evidence.

eventSequence, not device time, orders canonical local events. DEVICE_REPORTED time may be recorded as evidence but cannot establish trusted freshness or external chronology, and cannot silently control a freshness requirement that requires trusted external time. A proof obligation requiring trusted time remains UNKNOWN unless the permitted external time basis exists.

The permitted external time basis is governed by closed-loop-trusted-time/1. A VERIFIED_EXTERNAL time basis requires either a cryptographically verifiable external timestamp attestation, such as an RFC 3161 timestamp token, validated under a registered verification contract, or an attributable external-system record whose declared time authority the applicable proof obligation accepts. An unverified external time claim remains SOURCE_ASSERTED. Where neither basis exists, the obligation remains UNKNOWN.

artifacts
- ID: ARTIFACT_ID
- Global
- Policy: APPLICATION_DERIVED
- Application owns filename, type, version, size, hash, role, storage reference, availability, and notes.
- Every available artifact exposes individual retrieval.

The human interacts conversationally.

21.17 Verification timing fields

Every canonical test declares VERIFICATION_PHASE, EARLIEST_EXECUTABLE_STAGE, REQUIRED_BY_STAGE, PER_RUN_REQUIRED, FINAL_PRODUCT_REQUIRED, DELIVERY_REQUIRED, and TARGET_AVAILABILITY_CONDITION. The application validates these values against the test role and proof obligation and derives when execution is due.

29.12 Universal proposition state and three-valued logic

Every release-bearing proposition, applicability condition, independence condition, entailment conclusion, source-authenticity conclusion, environment claim, and external-capability claim carries truthValue TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN; epistemicBasis APPLICATION_OBSERVED, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL, EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED, SELF_ASSERTED, or NONE; currentScopeStatus CURRENT or STALE; freshnessStatus CURRENT, EXPIRED, UNKNOWN, or NOT_APPLICABLE; contradictionStatus CLEAR or CONTRADICTED; reasons; supportingEvidenceIds; and a derivation or accepted semantic-review identity.

TRUE requires affirmative support meeting the proof obligation. FALSE requires sufficient current evidence establishing noncompliance or negation. UNKNOWN applies when neither is established and fails closed wherever affirmative proof is required. Missing data is UNKNOWN unless a closed-universe rule affirmatively establishes FALSE. Contradictory sufficient evidence blocks and is never averaged away.

29.13 Proposition and proof-expression contract

Every normative requirement has one primary PROPOSITION_ID. Independent truth conditions are split or represented by one accepted acyclic proof expression. Semantic sameness is established only by an independent EQUIVALENT review; wording, embeddings, filenames, and hashes cannot merge propositions.

The closed proof-expression language permits LEAF, ALL_OF, ANY_OF, and AT_LEAST_K only. It has no arbitrary code, unrestricted negation, implicit coercion, stale references, or empty operators. ALL_OF is TRUE when all children are TRUE, FALSE when any is FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. ANY_OF is TRUE when any is TRUE, FALSE when all are FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. AT_LEAST_K is TRUE when trueCount ≥ K, FALSE when trueCount + unknownCount < K, and UNKNOWN otherwise.

Every current applicable release-bearing proposition has exactly one current PROOF_OBLIGATION_ID identifying its proof expression, required leaves, evidence classes, allowed epistemic bases, artifacts, dependencies, freshness, independence, verification timing, current satisfaction, blockers, and scope hash. Optional, advisory, stale, historical, or unregistered results cannot satisfy it.

EQUIVALENT applies only to proposition-to-proposition sameness. The relation between a test and a proof leaf, and between a proof expression and its proposition, is sufficiency, established by the accepted Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW. A LEAF references exactly one of: a canonical test with its required disposition, an observation-backed proposition, an applicability or activation condition, or a prerequisite proof obligation; each leaf declares its truth extraction, required evidence classes, and scope binding, and no other leaf target is valid in version 1. An ANY_OF expression is accepted only when the review establishes that each branch alone suffices to establish the parent proposition; an AT_LEAST_K expression is accepted only when every permitted K-combination suffices or an explicitly reviewed combinatorial sufficiency contract covers it. A branch that weakens proof strength is rejected at Stage 06.

29.14 Observation, entailment, origin, and freshness

Every release-bearing evidence path is EVIDENCE_RECORD → OBSERVATION_RECORD → proposition or proof leaf. An observation identifies exact subject, location or measurement point, finding, method/tool, inputs and outputs, hashes, origin, submitting actor, epistemic basis, time/freshness fields, source evidence, scope, and raw-response or native-execution provenance.

Every observation has an accepted relation ESTABLISHES, REFUTES, SUPPORTS_ONLY, CONTEXT_ONLY, DOES_NOT_ADDRESS, or UNKNOWN. Only ESTABLISHES provides affirmative proof; REFUTES provides failure evidence; SUPPORTS_ONLY and CONTEXT_ONLY cannot independently satisfy a proof obligation. Normalization never elevates an external claim.

Time-sensitive evidence records observedAt, its DEVICE_REPORTED, SOURCE_ASSERTED, or VERIFIED_EXTERNAL basis, validFrom, validUntil, supersession, freshness requirement, status, and reason. Required freshness that cannot be established is UNKNOWN. Current justificatory evidence is acyclic.

VERIFIED_EXTERNAL is achieved only under a registered attestation-verification contract fixing the evidence type, the attesting tool or system identity, the verification method, the bound inputs including the operation challengeNonce or reservation, the freshness rule, and the failure semantics. Absent such a registered contract, the basis remains EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED or weaker.

B. Insert after §21.17: target-availability reference contract

The authored form is records.<owning family>[i].fields.TARGET_AVAILABILITY_CONDITION = {"PROOF_EXPRESSION_ID": <reference>}. Here <reference> uses the existing response-local relationship convention: exactly {"tempKey":"<same-response proofExpressions tempKey>"} or {"recordId":"<current proofExpressions canonical ID supplied by the operation>"}, with no other keys, nulls or defaults. A tempKey must resolve uniquely to a proofExpressions proposal in the same response; a recordId must resolve to the correct current family, project and scope. The APPLICATION resolves this nested relationship through the single ingestion path and at proposal acceptance replaces <reference> with the allocated/resolved canonical ID string. Agents do not write the canonical string directly. This declares the nested relationship's placement, not a second ingestion path.

Stage 06 COMPLETE or RECONCILE_VERIFICATION_SUITE may admit structurally valid tests and their availability expressions together using existing proposal acceptance. Admission and canonical ID installation do not establish proof sufficiency. Pending PROOF_REVIEW blocks readiness/evaluation as accepted availability evidence, not initial authoring or proposal admission. Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW then assesses the installed exact expression and target proposition under the existing review contract; accepted current review permits evaluation. A failed review uses the existing reconciliation/replacement/invalidation lifecycle. No user-operated reference creation is required. The expression's proposition must be availability of the exact target identified by the owning obligation's current scope; the appropriate agent proposes its semantic meaning and composition, and the application validates it.

The expression uses only the existing LEAF, ALL_OF, ANY_OF and AT_LEAST_K language, existing valid leaf targets, evidence classes, truth extraction, accepted sufficiency review and current-scope bindings. It evaluates solely under §§29.12–29.14 and the target's existing byte/currentness/identity requirements. It must not depend on completion of the very execution whose availability it determines; ordinary acyclic prerequisite availability proof is permitted. A bare artifact record, filename, digest claim or phase label does not itself establish required byte availability. Missing, stale, unaccepted, circular or unresolved references cannot establish TRUE; apply the existing UNKNOWN/blocking rules without treating unknown as known absence. Closed-universe evidence is required to establish FALSE.

This reference does not change §16.1's due predicate or phase timing. No PHASE_TARGET, CURRENT_RECORD, VERIFIED_ARTIFACT_BYTES, or other additional condition-node grammar is introduced. An older representation may migrate only after a recorded lossless equivalence demonstration covering target, evidence, scope and TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN outcomes; otherwise affected timing/proofs remain stale pending reauthoring and review. Equivalence covers the whole effective predicate, including any separately applied phase-target constraints that the controlling source actually requires, not just the old serialized object. Existing compliant target/currentness/byte-observation functions and three-valued evaluators may be retained when their outputs are bound to the accepted existing proof contract and equivalence is demonstrated; old custom node objects are not admitted as a second canonical language. No pinned phase helper is grandfathered merely because it exists.

21.17 Verification timing fields

Every canonical test declares VERIFICATION_PHASE, EARLIEST_EXECUTABLE_STAGE, REQUIRED_BY_STAGE, PER_RUN_REQUIRED, FINAL_PRODUCT_REQUIRED, DELIVERY_REQUIRED, and TARGET_AVAILABILITY_CONDITION. The application validates these values against the test role and proof obligation and derives when execution is due.

29.12 Universal proposition state and three-valued logic

Every release-bearing proposition, applicability condition, independence condition, entailment conclusion, source-authenticity conclusion, environment claim, and external-capability claim carries truthValue TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN; epistemicBasis APPLICATION_OBSERVED, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL, EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED, SELF_ASSERTED, or NONE; currentScopeStatus CURRENT or STALE; freshnessStatus CURRENT, EXPIRED, UNKNOWN, or NOT_APPLICABLE; contradictionStatus CLEAR or CONTRADICTED; reasons; supportingEvidenceIds; and a derivation or accepted semantic-review identity.

TRUE requires affirmative support meeting the proof obligation. FALSE requires sufficient current evidence establishing noncompliance or negation. UNKNOWN applies when neither is established and fails closed wherever affirmative proof is required. Missing data is UNKNOWN unless a closed-universe rule affirmatively establishes FALSE. Contradictory sufficient evidence blocks and is never averaged away.

29.13 Proposition and proof-expression contract

Every normative requirement has one primary PROPOSITION_ID. Independent truth conditions are split or represented by one accepted acyclic proof expression. Semantic sameness is established only by an independent EQUIVALENT review; wording, embeddings, filenames, and hashes cannot merge propositions.

The closed proof-expression language permits LEAF, ALL_OF, ANY_OF, and AT_LEAST_K only. It has no arbitrary code, unrestricted negation, implicit coercion, stale references, or empty operators. ALL_OF is TRUE when all children are TRUE, FALSE when any is FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. ANY_OF is TRUE when any is TRUE, FALSE when all are FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. AT_LEAST_K is TRUE when trueCount ≥ K, FALSE when trueCount + unknownCount < K, and UNKNOWN otherwise.

Every current applicable release-bearing proposition has exactly one current PROOF_OBLIGATION_ID identifying its proof expression, required leaves, evidence classes, allowed epistemic bases, artifacts, dependencies, freshness, independence, verification timing, current satisfaction, blockers, and scope hash. Optional, advisory, stale, historical, or unregistered results cannot satisfy it.

EQUIVALENT applies only to proposition-to-proposition sameness. The relation between a test and a proof leaf, and between a proof expression and its proposition, is sufficiency, established by the accepted Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW. A LEAF references exactly one of: a canonical test with its required disposition, an observation-backed proposition, an applicability or activation condition, or a prerequisite proof obligation; each leaf declares its truth extraction, required evidence classes, and scope binding, and no other leaf target is valid in version 1. An ANY_OF expression is accepted only when the review establishes that each branch alone suffices to establish the parent proposition; an AT_LEAST_K expression is accepted only when every permitted K-combination suffices or an explicitly reviewed combinatorial sufficiency contract covers it. A branch that weakens proof strength is rejected at Stage 06.

29.14 Observation, entailment, origin, and freshness

Every release-bearing evidence path is EVIDENCE_RECORD → OBSERVATION_RECORD → proposition or proof leaf. An observation identifies exact subject, location or measurement point, finding, method/tool, inputs and outputs, hashes, origin, submitting actor, epistemic basis, time/freshness fields, source evidence, scope, and raw-response or native-execution provenance.

Every observation has an accepted relation ESTABLISHES, REFUTES, SUPPORTS_ONLY, CONTEXT_ONLY, DOES_NOT_ADDRESS, or UNKNOWN. Only ESTABLISHES provides affirmative proof; REFUTES provides failure evidence; SUPPORTS_ONLY and CONTEXT_ONLY cannot independently satisfy a proof obligation. Normalization never elevates an external claim.

Time-sensitive evidence records observedAt, its DEVICE_REPORTED, SOURCE_ASSERTED, or VERIFIED_EXTERNAL basis, validFrom, validUntil, supersession, freshness requirement, status, and reason. Required freshness that cannot be established is UNKNOWN. Current justificatory evidence is acyclic.

VERIFIED_EXTERNAL is achieved only under a registered attestation-verification contract fixing the evidence type, the attesting tool or system identity, the verification method, the bound inputs including the operation challengeNonce or reservation, the freshness rule, and the failure semantics. Absent such a registered contract, the basis remains EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED or weaker.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText:
21.17 Verification timing fields

Every canonical test declares VERIFICATION_PHASE, EARLIEST_EXECUTABLE_STAGE, REQUIRED_BY_STAGE, PER_RUN_REQUIRED, FINAL_PRODUCT_REQUIRED, DELIVERY_REQUIRED, and TARGET_AVAILABILITY_CONDITION. The application validates these values against the test role and proof obligation and derives when execution is due.

29.12 Universal proposition state and three-valued logic

Every release-bearing proposition, applicability condition, independence condition, entailment conclusion, source-authenticity conclusion, environment claim, and external-capability claim carries truthValue TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN; epistemicBasis APPLICATION_OBSERVED, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL, EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED, SELF_ASSERTED, or NONE; currentScopeStatus CURRENT or STALE; freshnessStatus CURRENT, EXPIRED, UNKNOWN, or NOT_APPLICABLE; contradictionStatus CLEAR or CONTRADICTED; reasons; supportingEvidenceIds; and a derivation or accepted semantic-review identity.

TRUE requires affirmative support meeting the proof obligation. FALSE requires sufficient current evidence establishing noncompliance or negation. UNKNOWN applies when neither is established and fails closed wherever affirmative proof is required. Missing data is UNKNOWN unless a closed-universe rule affirmatively establishes FALSE. Contradictory sufficient evidence blocks and is never averaged away.

29.13 Proposition and proof-expression contract

Every normative requirement has one primary PROPOSITION_ID. Independent truth conditions are split or represented by one accepted acyclic proof expression. Semantic sameness is established only by an independent EQUIVALENT review; wording, embeddings, filenames, and hashes cannot merge propositions.

The closed proof-expression language permits LEAF, ALL_OF, ANY_OF, and AT_LEAST_K only. It has no arbitrary code, unrestricted negation, implicit coercion, stale references, or empty operators. ALL_OF is TRUE when all children are TRUE, FALSE when any is FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. ANY_OF is TRUE when any is TRUE, FALSE when all are FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. AT_LEAST_K is TRUE when trueCount ≥ K, FALSE when trueCount + unknownCount < K, and UNKNOWN otherwise.

Every current applicable release-bearing proposition has exactly one current PROOF_OBLIGATION_ID identifying its proof expression, required leaves, evidence classes, allowed epistemic bases, artifacts, dependencies, freshness, independence, verification timing, current satisfaction, blockers, and scope hash. Optional, advisory, stale, historical, or unregistered results cannot satisfy it.

EQUIVALENT applies only to proposition-to-proposition sameness. The relation between a test and a proof leaf, and between a proof expression and its proposition, is sufficiency, established by the accepted Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW. A LEAF references exactly one of: a canonical test with its required disposition, an observation-backed proposition, an applicability or activation condition, or a prerequisite proof obligation; each leaf declares its truth extraction, required evidence classes, and scope binding, and no other leaf target is valid in version 1. An ANY_OF expression is accepted only when the review establishes that each branch alone suffices to establish the parent proposition; an AT_LEAST_K expression is accepted only when every permitted K-combination suffices or an explicitly reviewed combinatorial sufficiency contract covers it. A branch that weakens proof strength is rejected at Stage 06.

29.14 Observation, entailment, origin, and freshness

Every release-bearing evidence path is EVIDENCE_RECORD → OBSERVATION_RECORD → proposition or proof leaf. An observation identifies exact subject, location or measurement point, finding, method/tool, inputs and outputs, hashes, origin, submitting actor, epistemic basis, time/freshness fields, source evidence, scope, and raw-response or native-execution provenance.

Every observation has an accepted relation ESTABLISHES, REFUTES, SUPPORTS_ONLY, CONTEXT_ONLY, DOES_NOT_ADDRESS, or UNKNOWN. Only ESTABLISHES provides affirmative proof; REFUTES provides failure evidence; SUPPORTS_ONLY and CONTEXT_ONLY cannot independently satisfy a proof obligation. Normalization never elevates an external claim.

Time-sensitive evidence records observedAt, its DEVICE_REPORTED, SOURCE_ASSERTED, or VERIFIED_EXTERNAL basis, validFrom, validUntil, supersession, freshness requirement, status, and reason. Required freshness that cannot be established is UNKNOWN. Current justificatory evidence is acyclic.

VERIFIED_EXTERNAL is achieved only under a registered attestation-verification contract fixing the evidence type, the attesting tool or system identity, the verification method, the bound inputs including the operation challengeNonce or reservation, the freshness rule, and the failure semantics. Absent such a registered contract, the basis remains EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED or weaker.

21.17 Verification timing fields

Every canonical test declares VERIFICATION_PHASE, EARLIEST_EXECUTABLE_STAGE, REQUIRED_BY_STAGE, PER_RUN_REQUIRED, FINAL_PRODUCT_REQUIRED, DELIVERY_REQUIRED, and TARGET_AVAILABILITY_CONDITION. The application validates these values against the test role and proof obligation and derives when execution is due.

29.12 Universal proposition state and three-valued logic

Every release-bearing proposition, applicability condition, independence condition, entailment conclusion, source-authenticity conclusion, environment claim, and external-capability claim carries truthValue TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN; epistemicBasis APPLICATION_OBSERVED, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL, EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED, SELF_ASSERTED, or NONE; currentScopeStatus CURRENT or STALE; freshnessStatus CURRENT, EXPIRED, UNKNOWN, or NOT_APPLICABLE; contradictionStatus CLEAR or CONTRADICTED; reasons; supportingEvidenceIds; and a derivation or accepted semantic-review identity.

TRUE requires affirmative support meeting the proof obligation. FALSE requires sufficient current evidence establishing noncompliance or negation. UNKNOWN applies when neither is established and fails closed wherever affirmative proof is required. Missing data is UNKNOWN unless a closed-universe rule affirmatively establishes FALSE. Contradictory sufficient evidence blocks and is never averaged away.

29.13 Proposition and proof-expression contract

Every normative requirement has one primary PROPOSITION_ID. Independent truth conditions are split or represented by one accepted acyclic proof expression. Semantic sameness is established only by an independent EQUIVALENT review; wording, embeddings, filenames, and hashes cannot merge propositions.

The closed proof-expression language permits LEAF, ALL_OF, ANY_OF, and AT_LEAST_K only. It has no arbitrary code, unrestricted negation, implicit coercion, stale references, or empty operators. ALL_OF is TRUE when all children are TRUE, FALSE when any is FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. ANY_OF is TRUE when any is TRUE, FALSE when all are FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. AT_LEAST_K is TRUE when trueCount ≥ K, FALSE when trueCount + unknownCount < K, and UNKNOWN otherwise.

Every current applicable release-bearing proposition has exactly one current PROOF_OBLIGATION_ID identifying its proof expression, required leaves, evidence classes, allowed epistemic bases, artifacts, dependencies, freshness, independence, verification timing, current satisfaction, blockers, and scope hash. Optional, advisory, stale, historical, or unregistered results cannot satisfy it.

EQUIVALENT applies only to proposition-to-proposition sameness. The relation between a test and a proof leaf, and between a proof expression and its proposition, is sufficiency, established by the accepted Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW. A LEAF references exactly one of: a canonical test with its required disposition, an observation-backed proposition, an applicability or activation condition, or a prerequisite proof obligation; each leaf declares its truth extraction, required evidence classes, and scope binding, and no other leaf target is valid in version 1. An ANY_OF expression is accepted only when the review establishes that each branch alone suffices to establish the parent proposition; an AT_LEAST_K expression is accepted only when every permitted K-combination suffices or an explicitly reviewed combinatorial sufficiency contract covers it. A branch that weakens proof strength is rejected at Stage 06.

29.14 Observation, entailment, origin, and freshness

Every release-bearing evidence path is EVIDENCE_RECORD → OBSERVATION_RECORD → proposition or proof leaf. An observation identifies exact subject, location or measurement point, finding, method/tool, inputs and outputs, hashes, origin, submitting actor, epistemic basis, time/freshness fields, source evidence, scope, and raw-response or native-execution provenance.

Every observation has an accepted relation ESTABLISHES, REFUTES, SUPPORTS_ONLY, CONTEXT_ONLY, DOES_NOT_ADDRESS, or UNKNOWN. Only ESTABLISHES provides affirmative proof; REFUTES provides failure evidence; SUPPORTS_ONLY and CONTEXT_ONLY cannot independently satisfy a proof obligation. Normalization never elevates an external claim.

Time-sensitive evidence records observedAt, its DEVICE_REPORTED, SOURCE_ASSERTED, or VERIFIED_EXTERNAL basis, validFrom, validUntil, supersession, freshness requirement, status, and reason. Required freshness that cannot be established is UNKNOWN. Current justificatory evidence is acyclic.

VERIFIED_EXTERNAL is achieved only under a registered attestation-verification contract fixing the evidence type, the attesting tool or system identity, the verification method, the bound inputs including the operation challengeNonce or reservation, the freshness rule, and the failure semantics. Absent such a registered contract, the basis remains EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED or weaker.

The application validates these values against the test role and proof obligation and derives when execution is due.

29.12 Universal proposition state and three-valued logic

Every release-bearing proposition, applicability condition, independence condition, entailment conclusion, source-authenticity conclusion, environment claim, and external-capability claim carries truthValue TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN; epistemicBasis APPLICATION_OBSERVED, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL, EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED, SELF_ASSERTED, or NONE; currentScopeStatus CURRENT or STALE; freshnessStatus CURRENT, EXPIRED, UNKNOWN, or NOT_APPLICABLE; contradictionStatus CLEAR or CONTRADICTED; reasons; supportingEvidenceIds; and a derivation or accepted semantic-review identity.

TRUE requires affirmative support meeting the proof obligation. FALSE requires sufficient current evidence establishing noncompliance or negation. UNKNOWN applies when neither is established and fails closed wherever affirmative proof is required. Missing data is UNKNOWN unless a closed-universe rule affirmatively establishes FALSE. Contradictory sufficient evidence blocks and is never averaged away.

29.13 Proposition and proof-expression contract

Every normative requirement has one primary PROPOSITION_ID. Independent truth conditions are split or represented by one accepted acyclic proof expression. Semantic sameness is established only by an independent EQUIVALENT review; wording, embeddings, filenames, and hashes cannot merge propositions.

The closed proof-expression language permits LEAF, ALL_OF, ANY_OF, and AT_LEAST_K only. It has no arbitrary code, unrestricted negation, implicit coercion, stale references, or empty operators. ALL_OF is TRUE when all children are TRUE, FALSE when any is FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. ANY_OF is TRUE when any is TRUE, FALSE when all are FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. AT_LEAST_K is TRUE when trueCount ≥ K, FALSE when trueCount + unknownCount < K, and UNKNOWN otherwise.

Every current applicable release-bearing proposition has exactly one current PROOF_OBLIGATION_ID identifying its proof expression, required leaves, evidence classes, allowed epistemic bases, artifacts, dependencies, freshness, independence, verification timing, current satisfaction, blockers, and scope hash. Optional, advisory, stale, historical, or unregistered results cannot satisfy it.

EQUIVALENT applies only to proposition-to-proposition sameness. The relation between a test and a proof leaf, and between a proof expression and its proposition, is sufficiency, established by the accepted Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW. A LEAF references exactly one of: a canonical test with its required disposition, an observation-backed proposition, an applicability or activation condition, or a prerequisite proof obligation; each leaf declares its truth extraction, required evidence classes, and scope binding, and no other leaf target is valid in version 1. An ANY_OF expression is accepted only when the review establishes that each branch alone suffices to establish the parent proposition; an AT_LEAST_K expression is accepted only when every permitted K-combination suffices or an explicitly reviewed combinatorial sufficiency contract covers it. A branch that weakens proof strength is rejected at Stage 06.

29.14 Observation, entailment, origin, and freshness

Every release-bearing evidence path is EVIDENCE_RECORD → OBSERVATION_RECORD → proposition or proof leaf. An observation identifies exact subject, location or measurement point, finding, method/tool, inputs and outputs, hashes, origin, submitting actor, epistemic basis, time/freshness fields, source evidence, scope, and raw-response or native-execution provenance.

Every observation has an accepted relation ESTABLISHES, REFUTES, SUPPORTS_ONLY, CONTEXT_ONLY, DOES_NOT_ADDRESS, or UNKNOWN. Only ESTABLISHES provides affirmative proof; REFUTES provides failure evidence; SUPPORTS_ONLY and CONTEXT_ONLY cannot independently satisfy a proof obligation. Normalization never elevates an external claim.

Time-sensitive evidence records observedAt, its DEVICE_REPORTED, SOURCE_ASSERTED, or VERIFIED_EXTERNAL basis, validFrom, validUntil, supersession, freshness requirement, status, and reason. Required freshness that cannot be established is UNKNOWN. Current justificatory evidence is acyclic.

VERIFIED_EXTERNAL is achieved only under a registered attestation-verification contract fixing the evidence type, the attesting tool or system identity, the verification method, the bound inputs including the operation challengeNonce or reservation, the freshness rule, and the failure semantics. Absent such a registered contract, the basis remains EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED or weaker.

21.17 Verification timing fields

Every canonical test declares VERIFICATION_PHASE, EARLIEST_EXECUTABLE_STAGE, REQUIRED_BY_STAGE, PER_RUN_REQUIRED, FINAL_PRODUCT_REQUIRED, DELIVERY_REQUIRED, and TARGET_AVAILABILITY_CONDITION. The application validates these values against the test role and proof obligation and derives when execution is due.

29.12 Universal proposition state and three-valued logic

Every release-bearing proposition, applicability condition, independence condition, entailment conclusion, source-authenticity conclusion, environment claim, and external-capability claim carries truthValue TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN; epistemicBasis APPLICATION_OBSERVED, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL, EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED, SELF_ASSERTED, or NONE; currentScopeStatus CURRENT or STALE; freshnessStatus CURRENT, EXPIRED, UNKNOWN, or NOT_APPLICABLE; contradictionStatus CLEAR or CONTRADICTED; reasons; supportingEvidenceIds; and a derivation or accepted semantic-review identity.

TRUE requires affirmative support meeting the proof obligation. FALSE requires sufficient current evidence establishing noncompliance or negation. UNKNOWN applies when neither is established and fails closed wherever affirmative proof is required. Missing data is UNKNOWN unless a closed-universe rule affirmatively establishes FALSE. Contradictory sufficient evidence blocks and is never averaged away.

29.13 Proposition and proof-expression contract

Every normative requirement has one primary PROPOSITION_ID. Independent truth conditions are split or represented by one accepted acyclic proof expression. Semantic sameness is established only by an independent EQUIVALENT review; wording, embeddings, filenames, and hashes cannot merge propositions.

The closed proof-expression language permits LEAF, ALL_OF, ANY_OF, and AT_LEAST_K only. It has no arbitrary code, unrestricted negation, implicit coercion, stale references, or empty operators. ALL_OF is TRUE when all children are TRUE, FALSE when any is FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. ANY_OF is TRUE when any is TRUE, FALSE when all are FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. AT_LEAST_K is TRUE when trueCount ≥ K, FALSE when trueCount + unknownCount < K, and UNKNOWN otherwise.

Every current applicable release-bearing proposition has exactly one current PROOF_OBLIGATION_ID identifying its proof expression, required leaves, evidence classes, allowed epistemic bases, artifacts, dependencies, freshness, independence, verification timing, current satisfaction, blockers, and scope hash. Optional, advisory, stale, historical, or unregistered results cannot satisfy it.

EQUIVALENT applies only to proposition-to-proposition sameness. The relation between a test and a proof leaf, and between a proof expression and its proposition, is sufficiency, established by the accepted Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW. A LEAF references exactly one of: a canonical test with its required disposition, an observation-backed proposition, an applicability or activation condition, or a prerequisite proof obligation; each leaf declares its truth extraction, required evidence classes, and scope binding, and no other leaf target is valid in version 1. An ANY_OF expression is accepted only when the review establishes that each branch alone suffices to establish the parent proposition; an AT_LEAST_K expression is accepted only when every permitted K-combination suffices or an explicitly reviewed combinatorial sufficiency contract covers it. A branch that weakens proof strength is rejected at Stage 06.

29.14 Observation, entailment, origin, and freshness

Every release-bearing evidence path is EVIDENCE_RECORD → OBSERVATION_RECORD → proposition or proof leaf. An observation identifies exact subject, location or measurement point, finding, method/tool, inputs and outputs, hashes, origin, submitting actor, epistemic basis, time/freshness fields, source evidence, scope, and raw-response or native-execution provenance.

Every observation has an accepted relation ESTABLISHES, REFUTES, SUPPORTS_ONLY, CONTEXT_ONLY, DOES_NOT_ADDRESS, or UNKNOWN. Only ESTABLISHES provides affirmative proof; REFUTES provides failure evidence; SUPPORTS_ONLY and CONTEXT_ONLY cannot independently satisfy a proof obligation. Normalization never elevates an external claim.

Time-sensitive evidence records observedAt, its DEVICE_REPORTED, SOURCE_ASSERTED, or VERIFIED_EXTERNAL basis, validFrom, validUntil, supersession, freshness requirement, status, and reason. Required freshness that cannot be established is UNKNOWN. Current justificatory evidence is acyclic.

VERIFIED_EXTERNAL is achieved only under a registered attestation-verification contract fixing the evidence type, the attesting tool or system identity, the verification method, the bound inputs including the operation challengeNonce or reservation, the freshness rule, and the failure semantics. Absent such a registered contract, the basis remains EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED or weaker.

Equivalence covers the whole effective predicate, including any separately applied phase-target constraints that the controlling source actually requires, not just the old serialized object. Existing compliant target/currentness/byte-observation functions and three-valued evaluators may be retained when their outputs are bound to the accepted existing proof contract and equivalence is demonstrated; old custom node objects are not admitted as a second canonical language. No pinned phase helper is grandfathered merely because it exists.

21.17 Verification timing fields

Every canonical test declares VERIFICATION_PHASE, EARLIEST_EXECUTABLE_STAGE, REQUIRED_BY_STAGE, PER_RUN_REQUIRED, FINAL_PRODUCT_REQUIRED, DELIVERY_REQUIRED, and TARGET_AVAILABILITY_CONDITION. The application validates these values against the test role and proof obligation and derives when execution is due.

29.12 Universal proposition state and three-valued logic

Every release-bearing proposition, applicability condition, independence condition, entailment conclusion, source-authenticity conclusion, environment claim, and external-capability claim carries truthValue TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN; epistemicBasis APPLICATION_OBSERVED, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL, EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED, SELF_ASSERTED, or NONE; currentScopeStatus CURRENT or STALE; freshnessStatus CURRENT, EXPIRED, UNKNOWN, or NOT_APPLICABLE; contradictionStatus CLEAR or CONTRADICTED; reasons; supportingEvidenceIds; and a derivation or accepted semantic-review identity.

TRUE requires affirmative support meeting the proof obligation. FALSE requires sufficient current evidence establishing noncompliance or negation. UNKNOWN applies when neither is established and fails closed wherever affirmative proof is required. Missing data is UNKNOWN unless a closed-universe rule affirmatively establishes FALSE. Contradictory sufficient evidence blocks and is never averaged away.

29.13 Proposition and proof-expression contract

Every normative requirement has one primary PROPOSITION_ID. Independent truth conditions are split or represented by one accepted acyclic proof expression. Semantic sameness is established only by an independent EQUIVALENT review; wording, embeddings, filenames, and hashes cannot merge propositions.

The closed proof-expression language permits LEAF, ALL_OF, ANY_OF, and AT_LEAST_K only. It has no arbitrary code, unrestricted negation, implicit coercion, stale references, or empty operators. ALL_OF is TRUE when all children are TRUE, FALSE when any is FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. ANY_OF is TRUE when any is TRUE, FALSE when all are FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. AT_LEAST_K is TRUE when trueCount ≥ K, FALSE when trueCount + unknownCount < K, and UNKNOWN otherwise.

Every current applicable release-bearing proposition has exactly one current PROOF_OBLIGATION_ID identifying its proof expression, required leaves, evidence classes, allowed epistemic bases, artifacts, dependencies, freshness, independence, verification timing, current satisfaction, blockers, and scope hash. Optional, advisory, stale, historical, or unregistered results cannot satisfy it.

EQUIVALENT applies only to proposition-to-proposition sameness. The relation between a test and a proof leaf, and between a proof expression and its proposition, is sufficiency, established by the accepted Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW. A LEAF references exactly one of: a canonical test with its required disposition, an observation-backed proposition, an applicability or activation condition, or a prerequisite proof obligation; each leaf declares its truth extraction, required evidence classes, and scope binding, and no other leaf target is valid in version 1. An ANY_OF expression is accepted only when the review establishes that each branch alone suffices to establish the parent proposition; an AT_LEAST_K expression is accepted only when every permitted K-combination suffices or an explicitly reviewed combinatorial sufficiency contract covers it. A branch that weakens proof strength is rejected at Stage 06.

29.14 Observation, entailment, origin, and freshness

Every release-bearing evidence path is EVIDENCE_RECORD → OBSERVATION_RECORD → proposition or proof leaf. An observation identifies exact subject, location or measurement point, finding, method/tool, inputs and outputs, hashes, origin, submitting actor, epistemic basis, time/freshness fields, source evidence, scope, and raw-response or native-execution provenance.

Every observation has an accepted relation ESTABLISHES, REFUTES, SUPPORTS_ONLY, CONTEXT_ONLY, DOES_NOT_ADDRESS, or UNKNOWN. Only ESTABLISHES provides affirmative proof; REFUTES provides failure evidence; SUPPORTS_ONLY and CONTEXT_ONLY cannot independently satisfy a proof obligation. Normalization never elevates an external claim.

Time-sensitive evidence records observedAt, its DEVICE_REPORTED, SOURCE_ASSERTED, or VERIFIED_EXTERNAL basis, validFrom, validUntil, supersession, freshness requirement, status, and reason. Required freshness that cannot be established is UNKNOWN. Current justificatory evidence is acyclic.

VERIFIED_EXTERNAL is achieved only under a registered attestation-verification contract fixing the evidence type, the attesting tool or system identity, the verification method, the bound inputs including the operation challengeNonce or reservation, the freshness rule, and the failure semantics. Absent such a registered contract, the basis remains EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED or weaker.

Closed-universe evidence is required to establish FALSE.

An observation identifies exact subject, location or measurement point, finding, method/tool, inputs and outputs, hashes, origin, submitting actor, epistemic basis, time/freshness fields, source evidence, scope, and raw-response or native-execution provenance.

Every observation has an accepted relation ESTABLISHES, REFUTES, SUPPORTS_ONLY, CONTEXT_ONLY, DOES_NOT_ADDRESS, or UNKNOWN. Only ESTABLISHES provides affirmative proof; REFUTES provides failure evidence; SUPPORTS_ONLY and CONTEXT_ONLY cannot independently satisfy a proof obligation. Normalization never elevates an external claim.

Time-sensitive evidence records observedAt, its DEVICE_REPORTED, SOURCE_ASSERTED, or VERIFIED_EXTERNAL basis, validFrom, validUntil, supersession, freshness requirement, status, and reason. Required freshness that cannot be established is UNKNOWN. Current justificatory evidence is acyclic.

VERIFIED_EXTERNAL is achieved only under a registered attestation-verification contract fixing the evidence type, the attesting tool or system identity, the verification method, the bound inputs including the operation challengeNonce or reservation, the freshness rule, and the failure semantics. Absent such a registered contract, the basis remains EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED or weaker.

proofExpressions
- ID: PROOF_EXPRESSION_ID
- Stage: 6
- Policy: REPLACE_CURRENT_STAGE_SET
- AGENT owns proposed semantic composition; APPLICATION owns normalized closed expression, validation, identity, review relationships, scope, hash, and evaluation.

proofObligations
- ID: PROOF_OBLIGATION_ID
- Stage: 6 and recalculated as dependencies change
- Policy: APPLICATION_DERIVED
- APPLICATION owns every field, including verification phase, due-stage fields, evidence requirements, allowed epistemic bases, activation leaves, dependencies, expression, satisfaction state, and blockers.
B. Insert after §21.17: target-availability reference contract

TARGET_AVAILABILITY_CONDITION is a required, non-null closed canonical object with exactly one required non-null property PROOF_EXPRESSION_ID, a canonical proofExpressions ID string. It is one immutable owning-record-to-proofExpressions relationship, with no default. Its producer, scope, writable operation and invalidation owner follow the owning record's existing proposal/acceptance contract; the APPLICATION alone resolves and installs the canonical relationship. It is stored on that existing record, not in a new family.

The authored form is records.<owning family>[i].fields.TARGET_AVAILABILITY_CONDITION = {"PROOF_EXPRESSION_ID": <reference>}. Here <reference> uses the existing response-local relationship convention: exactly {"tempKey":"<same-response proofExpressions tempKey>"} or {"recordId":"<current proofExpressions canonical ID supplied by the operation>"}, with no other keys, nulls or defaults. A tempKey must resolve uniquely to a proofExpressions proposal in the same response; a recordId must resolve to the correct current family, project and scope. The APPLICATION resolves this nested relationship through the single ingestion path and at proposal acceptance replaces <reference> with the allocated/resolved canonical ID string. Agents do not write the canonical string directly. This declares the nested relationship's placement, not a second ingestion path.

Stage 06 COMPLETE or RECONCILE_VERIFICATION_SUITE may admit structurally valid tests and their availability expressions together using existing proposal acceptance. Admission and canonical ID installation do not establish proof sufficiency. Pending PROOF_REVIEW blocks readiness/evaluation as accepted availability evidence, not initial authoring or proposal admission. Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW then assesses the installed exact expression and target proposition under the existing review contract; accepted current review permits evaluation. A failed review uses the existing reconciliation/replacement/invalidation lifecycle. No user-operated reference creation is required. The expression's proposition must be availability of the exact target identified by the owning obligation's current scope; the appropriate agent proposes its semantic meaning and composition, and the application validates it.

The expression uses only the existing LEAF, ALL_OF, ANY_OF and AT_LEAST_K language, existing valid leaf targets, evidence classes, truth extraction, accepted sufficiency review and current-scope bindings. It evaluates solely under §§29.12–29.14 and the target's existing byte/currentness/identity requirements. It must not depend on completion of the very execution whose availability it determines; ordinary acyclic prerequisite availability proof is permitted. A bare artifact record, filename, digest claim or phase label does not itself establish required byte availability. Missing, stale, unaccepted, circular or unresolved references cannot establish TRUE; apply the existing UNKNOWN/blocking rules without treating unknown as known absence. Closed-universe evidence is required to establish FALSE.

21.3 Canonical structure and dataflow

Test IR is a topologically ordered directed acyclic graph. Every step has a unique application-validated stepId, one registered op, and an explicit inputs object. Each input references exactly one literal, immutable binding, or prior step output. A step may reference only an earlier step. Hidden accumulators, implicit stacks, ambient project state, ambient current values, operand-by-position rules, and implementation-dependent input selection are prohibited.

Every registered operation declares named input ports, output ports, exact types, cardinalities, deterministic error codes, error propagation, and resource-cost category. Each operation declares exact input arity and types and one normalized output type. Multi-artifact branches use explicit step references. BYTE_COMPARE and COMPARE receive explicit left and right inputs. Assertions receive explicit actual and expected inputs. A failed or unknown predecessor prevents dependent execution and propagates the registered terminal disposition without partial canonical result; errors propagate as typed execution failure and no later step may consume a failed output. Intermediate step outputs exist only for the current execution unless explicitly emitted as observations or evidence.
D. Insert after §21.17: residual native semantics

Remaining result-bearing argument/output closure: BYTE_COMPARE is exact length-and-byte equality of two byte inputs, with no ordering/operator default. ASSERT_MATCH asserts the same Boolean regex result as REGEX using actual/pattern/optional flags; ordered assertions use the exact ordering above. Each assertion yields only SATISFIED or VIOLATED on valid data, with other terminal dispositions propagated as D5 states. The optional message on assertions is a non-null string, absent by default, used only as diagnostic text and never to alter a result. SORT/UNIQUE require arrays and return arrays; MIN/MAX/SUM require arrays as stated. HASH_SHA256 requires bytes; REGEX requires string value/pattern; selectors require a string path and the defined structured value. Unknown optional arguments and implicit operand/binding selection are prohibited. Authoring shortcuts remain permitted only when they compile to the identical explicit §21.3 DAG and named ports. No extra primitive, alternate successful result type or undeclared default is authorized by registry publication. These additions close the result-bearing choices identified in the bounded argument/port omission comparison; the full generated registry still receives the independent §§2.2/14.5 review.

Unsupported definition syntax, unknown arguments/operations and invalid declared types reject Stage 06 ingestion. Missing required material before execution is BLOCKED. Once started, invalid/unrepresentable data, no-match selection, empty required aggregate, numeric overflow or unsupported precision yields UNDETERMINED; runtime limit/platform/worker failure yields EXECUTION_FAILED. A dependency cannot consume an error or partial output. The operation registry declares deterministic typed codes for these categories; wording is not a new semantic contract. Apply §21.16 to every affected language/parser/selector/operation identity. No existing digest is endorsed by this amendment, and no same-identity incompatible runtime is permitted.

Each input references exactly one literal, immutable binding, or prior step output. A step may reference only an earlier step. Hidden accumulators, implicit stacks, ambient project state, ambient current values, operand-by-position rules, and implementation-dependent input selection are prohibited.

Every registered operation declares named input ports, output ports, exact types, cardinalities, deterministic error codes, error propagation, and resource-cost category. Each operation declares exact input arity and types and one normalized output type. Multi-artifact branches use explicit step references. BYTE_COMPARE and COMPARE receive explicit left and right inputs. Assertions receive explicit actual and expected inputs. A failed or unknown predecessor prevents dependent execution and propagates the registered terminal disposition without partial canonical result; errors propagate as typed execution failure and no later step may consume a failed output. Intermediate step outputs exist only for the current execution unless explicitly emitted as observations or evidence.

Unsupported definition syntax, unknown arguments/operations and invalid declared types reject Stage 06 ingestion. Missing required material before execution is BLOCKED. Once started, invalid/unrepresentable data, no-match selection, empty required aggregate, numeric overflow or unsupported precision yields UNDETERMINED; runtime limit/platform/worker failure yields EXECUTION_FAILED. A dependency cannot consume an error or partial output. The operation registry declares deterministic typed codes for these categories; wording is not a new semantic contract.
