Test IR is a topologically ordered directed acyclic graph. Every step has a unique application-validated stepId, one registered op, and an explicit inputs object. Each input references exactly one literal, immutable binding, or prior step output. A step may reference only an earlier step. Hidden accumulators, implicit stacks, ambient project state, ambient current values, operand-by-position rules, and implementation-dependent input selection are prohibited.

Every registered operation declares named input ports, output ports, exact types, cardinalities, deterministic error codes, error propagation, and resource-cost category. Each operation declares exact input arity and types and one normalized output type. Multi-artifact branches use explicit step references. BYTE_COMPARE and COMPARE receive explicit left and right inputs. Assertions receive explicit actual and expected inputs. A failed or unknown predecessor prevents dependent execution and propagates the registered terminal disposition without partial canonical result; errors propagate as typed execution failure and no later step may consume a failed output. Intermediate step outputs exist only for the current execution unless explicitly emitted as observations or evidence.
D. Insert after §21.17: residual native semantics
D2. Numbers.

Unsupported definition syntax, unknown arguments/operations and invalid declared types reject Stage 06 ingestion. Missing required material before execution is BLOCKED. Once started, invalid/unrepresentable data, no-match selection, empty required aggregate, numeric overflow or unsupported precision yields UNDETERMINED; runtime limit/platform/worker failure yields EXECUTION_FAILED. A dependency cannot consume an error or partial output. The operation registry declares deterministic typed codes for these categories; wording is not a new semantic contract. Apply §21.16 to every affected language/parser/selector/operation identity. No existing digest is endorsed by this amendment, and no same-identity incompatible runtime is permitted.

These clauses close result-bearing primitive/parser choices, not replace §§21.1–21.17. Named ports, DAG validation, immutable bindings, prohibited execution, limits and required identities remain as already specified. Unless expressly defaulted below, an omitted required argument is invalid; no coercion supplies it. The published registry must encode these rules exactly.

Remaining result-bearing argument/output closure: BYTE_COMPARE is exact length-and-byte equality of two byte inputs, with no ordering/operator default. ASSERT_MATCH asserts the same Boolean regex result as REGEX using actual/pattern/optional flags; ordered assertions use the exact ordering above. Each assertion yields only SATISFIED or VIOLATED on valid data, with other terminal dispositions propagated as D5 states. The optional message on assertions is a non-null string, absent by default, used only as diagnostic text and never to alter a result. SORT/UNIQUE require arrays and return arrays; MIN/MAX/SUM require arrays as stated. HASH_SHA256 requires bytes; REGEX requires string value/pattern; selectors require a string path and the defined structured value. Unknown optional arguments and implicit operand/binding selection are prohibited. Authoring shortcuts remain permitted only when they compile to the identical explicit §21.3 DAG and named ports. No extra primitive, alternate successful result type or undeclared default is authorized by registry publication. These additions close the result-bearing choices identified in the bounded argument/port omission comparison; the full generated registry still receives the independent §§2.2/14.5 review.

COMPARE has optional operator with exact enum EQ, NE, GT, GTE, LT, LTE and default EQ. Its optional numericMode has exactly INTEGER, DECIMAL_STRING, APPROXIMATE; omission means the ordinary exact comparison described below, with no mode inferred from tolerance presence. ASSERT_EQ accepts the same optional numericMode and tolerances. No other assertion accepts numericMode or tolerances. Explicit INTEGER remains accepted and preserves ordinary exact comparison: canonical equality for nonnumeric canonical values, and safe-integer equality if either operand is a JSON number (then both must be safe integers). The name INTEGER does not coerce strings or prohibit ordinary nonnumeric canonical equality. Omitted mode follows the same rule. NE is the logical complement of EQ under the selected mode; invalid operands do not become a true NE.

DECIMAL_STRING equality requires two plain decimal strings matching [+-]?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)? after removal of surrounding ASCII U+0009–U+000D/U+0020 whitespace; compare mathematically exactly, ignoring leading plus/zeros and trailing fractional zeros. Ordered COMPARE operators and ASSERT_GT/GTE/LT/LTE use exact ordering of two safe integers or two such decimal strings. COMPARE with ordered operators accepts omitted mode or INTEGER for that ordinary exact domain; explicit DECIMAL_STRING restricts both operands to those strings. Ordered comparisons reject APPROXIMATE and every tolerance argument at definition admission. All EQ/NE/ASSERT_EQ comparisons outside APPROXIMATE also reject tolerance arguments, including compatibility aliases. No binary-float approximation or exponent is implicit.

APPROXIMATE applies only to COMPARE EQ/NE or ASSERT_EQ and requires an explicit absTol or relTol (or its compatibility alias). Operands and tolerances accept a JSON safe integer other than negative zero, a canonical plain decimal string as just defined, or that exact typed DECIMAL object. Operands may be negative; tolerances must be mathematically nonnegative. At least one tolerance component is explicit; the omitted component is zero. Use exact arithmetic: |actual-expected| <= max(absTol, relTol × max(|actual|,|expected|)). Approximate NE is the logical complement of that equality result. Compatibility names absoluteTolerance and relativeTolerance map to absTol and relTol; when both names for a component appear they must normalize to exactly the same mathematical value, otherwise reject the definition. Unsupported precision is UNDETERMINED. These aliases authorize no other default.

conditions: Applies to the closed native Test IR definition and execution domains; admission validation, valid-data output semantics and execution dispositions remain distinct. Existing DAG, named ports, immutable bindings, safe execution and identity requirements govern.

statement: value is a string matching -?(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(\.[0-9]+)? whose mathematical value is not negative zero.

primarySourceLocation.controllingText: The exact typed DECIMAL representation is a closed object with exactly the two required non-null keys numberType and value: numberType is the string DECIMAL; value is a string matching -?(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(\.[0-9]+)? whose mathematical value is not negative zero. Fractional trailing zeros are accepted; an empty fractional part, plus, whitespace, exponent, leading integer zeros, nulls, extra keys, and numeric value in place of the string are rejected. This same decimal-text grammar is used for canonical plain decimal strings in APPROXIMATE; it is deliberately stricter than DECIMAL_STRING mode. SORT's DECIMAL domain requires these typed objects, compares mathematical values exactly, and preserves each original object; it does not rewrite equivalent decimal spellings. Safe-integer numeric values belong to SORT INTEGER, not DECIMAL.

21.3 Canonical structure and dataflow

Test IR is a topologically ordered directed acyclic graph. Every step has a unique application-validated stepId, one registered op, and an explicit inputs object. Each input references exactly one literal, immutable binding, or prior step output. A step may reference only an earlier step. Hidden accumulators, implicit stacks, ambient project state, ambient current values, operand-by-position rules, and implementation-dependent input selection are prohibited.

Every registered operation declares named input ports, output ports, exact types, cardinalities, deterministic error codes, error propagation, and resource-cost category. Each operation declares exact input arity and types and one normalized output type. Multi-artifact branches use explicit step references. BYTE_COMPARE and COMPARE receive explicit left and right inputs. Assertions receive explicit actual and expected inputs. A failed or unknown predecessor prevents dependent execution and propagates the registered terminal disposition without partial canonical result; errors propagate as typed execution failure and no later step may consume a failed output. Intermediate step outputs exist only for the current execution unless explicitly emitted as observations or evidence.
D. Insert after §21.17: residual native semantics
D3. Selectors.

PARSE_XML returns the document element as a canonical JSON object with exactly four required non-null properties: name (exact element-name string), attributes (object of exact parsed attribute-name/string-value pairs), children (ordered array of its immediate element-node values), and content (ordered array of strings and immediate element-node values in source content order). Every child appears once in children and once as the same canonical value in content; this is duplicated value content, not a cyclic pointer or identity-based equality. Each nonempty ordinary text run between markup boundaries contributes one decoded string; each nonempty CDATA body contributes one literal string. Empty runs are omitted, comments contribute no entry, adjacent strings separated by comment/CDATA boundaries are not coalesced, and entity references within a text run are decoded into that one string. Outside-root whitespace and the declaration are not represented. Attribute order has no canonical-equality significance; child/content array order and text-run segmentation do. Thus differently ordered attributes with equal values compare equal, while mixed text/child content remains observable in exact document order. XML name/attribute/character normalization is precisely the parsing rule above, not namespace inference.

Unsupported definition syntax, unknown arguments/operations and invalid declared types reject Stage 06 ingestion. Missing required material before execution is BLOCKED. Once started, invalid/unrepresentable data, no-match selection, empty required aggregate, numeric overflow or unsupported precision yields UNDETERMINED; runtime limit/platform/worker failure yields EXECUTION_FAILED. A dependency cannot consume an error or partial output. The operation registry declares deterministic typed codes for these categories; wording is not a new semantic contract. Apply §21.16 to every affected language/parser/selector/operation identity. No existing digest is endorsed by this amendment, and no same-identity incompatible runtime is permitted.

These clauses close result-bearing primitive/parser choices, not replace §§21.1–21.17. Named ports, DAG validation, immutable bindings, prohibited execution, limits and required identities remain as already specified. Unless expressly defaulted below, an omitted required argument is invalid; no coercion supplies it. The published registry must encode these rules exactly.

Remaining result-bearing argument/output closure: BYTE_COMPARE is exact length-and-byte equality of two byte inputs, with no ordering/operator default. ASSERT_MATCH asserts the same Boolean regex result as REGEX using actual/pattern/optional flags; ordered assertions use the exact ordering above. Each assertion yields only SATISFIED or VIOLATED on valid data, with other terminal dispositions propagated as D5 states. The optional message on assertions is a non-null string, absent by default, used only as diagnostic text and never to alter a result. SORT/UNIQUE require arrays and return arrays; MIN/MAX/SUM require arrays as stated. HASH_SHA256 requires bytes; REGEX requires string value/pattern; selectors require a string path and the defined structured value. Unknown optional arguments and implicit operand/binding selection are prohibited. Authoring shortcuts remain permitted only when they compile to the identical explicit §21.3 DAG and named ports. No extra primitive, alternate successful result type or undeclared default is authorized by registry publication. These additions close the result-bearing choices identified in the bounded argument/port omission comparison; the full generated registry still receives the independent §§2.2/14.5 review.

PARSE_XML supports the XML 1.0 UTF-8 subset with one root, scalar-valid XML characters, the element/attribute name grammar above, quoted unique attributes, matching tags, comments, CDATA, the five predefined entities and legal decimal/hex numeric character references. An optional initial declaration states version 1.0, optional encoding UTF-8 and optional standalone yes/no in that order. CRLF and CR normalize to LF; literal attribute tab/newline/CR normalize to spaces, while numeric character references preserve their referenced character. DTDs, custom entities, processing instructions, namespace expansion and unsupported declarations are not native semantics. Names containing a colon remain literal names, not namespace-resolved names. Comments do not enter text() output; CDATA does. Invalid/unsupported content cannot yield a successful partial parse.

These canonical node values may be consumed by canonical equality, UNIQUE, ASSERT_SET_EQUAL and SELECT_JSON_PATH without opaque host-object behavior. For JSON-path traversal their object keys, including attributes, use §34.1 key order; XML traversal uses children/content source order. SELECT_XML requires a parsed node value from PARSE_XML or a node selected from that parsed value in the same execution; a lookalike authored JSON object does not acquire XML-node provenance. Provenance does not affect canonical equality. Its input is one node, not an implicitly unwrapped array; extraction from an element-result array is explicit through SELECT_JSON_PATH.

Every child appears once in children and once as the same canonical value in content; this is duplicated value content, not a cyclic pointer or identity-based equality. Each nonempty ordinary text run between markup boundaries contributes one decoded string; each nonempty CDATA body contributes one literal string. Empty runs are omitted, comments contribute no entry, adjacent strings separated by comment/CDATA boundaries are not coalesced, and entity references within a text run are decoded into that one string. Outside-root whitespace and the declaration are not represented. Attribute order has no canonical-equality significance; child/content array order and text-run segmentation do. Thus differently ordered attributes with equal values compare equal, while mixed text/child content remains observable in exact document order. XML name/attribute/character normalization is precisely the parsing rule above, not namespace inference.

21.3 Canonical structure and dataflow

Test IR is a topologically ordered directed acyclic graph. Every step has a unique application-validated stepId, one registered op, and an explicit inputs object. Each input references exactly one literal, immutable binding, or prior step output. A step may reference only an earlier step. Hidden accumulators, implicit stacks, ambient project state, ambient current values, operand-by-position rules, and implementation-dependent input selection are prohibited.

Every registered operation declares named input ports, output ports, exact types, cardinalities, deterministic error codes, error propagation, and resource-cost category. Each operation declares exact input arity and types and one normalized output type. Multi-artifact branches use explicit step references. BYTE_COMPARE and COMPARE receive explicit left and right inputs. Assertions receive explicit actual and expected inputs. A failed or unknown predecessor prevents dependent execution and propagates the registered terminal disposition without partial canonical result; errors propagate as typed execution failure and no later step may consume a failed output. Intermediate step outputs exist only for the current execution unless explicitly emitted as observations or evidence.
D. Insert after §21.17: residual native semantics
D4. Text, CSV, XML and regex.

Unsupported definition syntax, unknown arguments/operations and invalid declared types reject Stage 06 ingestion. Missing required material before execution is BLOCKED. Once started, invalid/unrepresentable data, no-match selection, empty required aggregate, numeric overflow or unsupported precision yields UNDETERMINED; runtime limit/platform/worker failure yields EXECUTION_FAILED. A dependency cannot consume an error or partial output. The operation registry declares deterministic typed codes for these categories; wording is not a new semantic contract. Apply §21.16 to every affected language/parser/selector/operation identity. No existing digest is endorsed by this amendment, and no same-identity incompatible runtime is permitted.

These clauses close result-bearing primitive/parser choices, not replace §§21.1–21.17. Named ports, DAG validation, immutable bindings, prohibited execution, limits and required identities remain as already specified. Unless expressly defaulted below, an omitted required argument is invalid; no coercion supplies it. The published registry must encode these rules exactly.

Remaining result-bearing argument/output closure: BYTE_COMPARE is exact length-and-byte equality of two byte inputs, with no ordering/operator default. ASSERT_MATCH asserts the same Boolean regex result as REGEX using actual/pattern/optional flags; ordered assertions use the exact ordering above. Each assertion yields only SATISFIED or VIOLATED on valid data, with other terminal dispositions propagated as D5 states. The optional message on assertions is a non-null string, absent by default, used only as diagnostic text and never to alter a result. SORT/UNIQUE require arrays and return arrays; MIN/MAX/SUM require arrays as stated. HASH_SHA256 requires bytes; REGEX requires string value/pattern; selectors require a string path and the defined structured value. Unknown optional arguments and implicit operand/binding selection are prohibited. Authoring shortcuts remain permitted only when they compile to the identical explicit §21.3 DAG and named ports. No extra primitive, alternate successful result type or undeclared default is authorized by registry publication. These additions close the result-bearing choices identified in the bounded argument/port omission comparison; the full generated registry still receives the independent §§2.2/14.5 review.

XML selectors start with exactly one slash, then child-element segments named [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]* or *, optionally followed by [positive safe integer]. The first segment matches the document element at position 1; later positions apply within each parent's matching child elements. Only the final segment may be @name or text(). Element results are arrays of the canonical element-node values defined in D4; attribute results are arrays of existing exact attribute strings; text() returns one string per selected element, concatenating descendant text/CDATA in document order and excluding comments. A wholly empty selection at any segment, including a final attribute selection, is UNDETERMINED. A selected element with no text yields the known empty string, not a missing selection. Other selector syntax is invalid before execution.

PARSE_XML supports the XML 1.0 UTF-8 subset with one root, scalar-valid XML characters, the element/attribute name grammar above, quoted unique attributes, matching tags, comments, CDATA, the five predefined entities and legal decimal/hex numeric character references. An optional initial declaration states version 1.0, optional encoding UTF-8 and optional standalone yes/no in that order. CRLF and CR normalize to LF; literal attribute tab/newline/CR normalize to spaces, while numeric character references preserve their referenced character. DTDs, custom entities, processing instructions, namespace expansion and unsupported declarations are not native semantics. Names containing a colon remain literal names, not namespace-resolved names. Comments do not enter text() output; CDATA does. Invalid/unsupported content cannot yield a successful partial parse.

These canonical node values may be consumed by canonical equality, UNIQUE, ASSERT_SET_EQUAL and SELECT_JSON_PATH without opaque host-object behavior. For JSON-path traversal their object keys, including attributes, use §34.1 key order; XML traversal uses children/content source order. SELECT_XML requires a parsed node value from PARSE_XML or a node selected from that parsed value in the same execution; a lookalike authored JSON object does not acquire XML-node provenance. Provenance does not affect canonical equality. Its input is one node, not an implicitly unwrapped array; extraction from an element-result array is explicit through SELECT_JSON_PATH.

21.3 Canonical structure and dataflow

Test IR is a topologically ordered directed acyclic graph. Every step has a unique application-validated stepId, one registered op, and an explicit inputs object. Each input references exactly one literal, immutable binding, or prior step output. A step may reference only an earlier step. Hidden accumulators, implicit stacks, ambient project state, ambient current values, operand-by-position rules, and implementation-dependent input selection are prohibited.

Every registered operation declares named input ports, output ports, exact types, cardinalities, deterministic error codes, error propagation, and resource-cost category. Each operation declares exact input arity and types and one normalized output type. Multi-artifact branches use explicit step references. BYTE_COMPARE and COMPARE receive explicit left and right inputs. Assertions receive explicit actual and expected inputs. A failed or unknown predecessor prevents dependent execution and propagates the registered terminal disposition without partial canonical result; errors propagate as typed execution failure and no later step may consume a failed output. Intermediate step outputs exist only for the current execution unless explicitly emitted as observations or evidence.
D. Insert after §21.17: residual native semantics
D4. Text, CSV, XML and regex.

PARSE_XML returns the document element as a canonical JSON object with exactly four required non-null properties: name (exact element-name string), attributes (object of exact parsed attribute-name/string-value pairs), children (ordered array of its immediate element-node values), and content (ordered array of strings and immediate element-node values in source content order). Every child appears once in children and once as the same canonical value in content; this is duplicated value content, not a cyclic pointer or identity-based equality. Each nonempty ordinary text run between markup boundaries contributes one decoded string; each nonempty CDATA body contributes one literal string. Empty runs are omitted, comments contribute no entry, adjacent strings separated by comment/CDATA boundaries are not coalesced, and entity references within a text run are decoded into that one string. Outside-root whitespace and the declaration are not represented. Attribute order has no canonical-equality significance; child/content array order and text-run segmentation do. Thus differently ordered attributes with equal values compare equal, while mixed text/child content remains observable in exact document order. XML name/attribute/character normalization is precisely the parsing rule above, not namespace inference.

Unsupported definition syntax, unknown arguments/operations and invalid declared types reject Stage 06 ingestion. Missing required material before execution is BLOCKED. Once started, invalid/unrepresentable data, no-match selection, empty required aggregate, numeric overflow or unsupported precision yields UNDETERMINED; runtime limit/platform/worker failure yields EXECUTION_FAILED. A dependency cannot consume an error or partial output. The operation registry declares deterministic typed codes for these categories; wording is not a new semantic contract. Apply §21.16 to every affected language/parser/selector/operation identity. No existing digest is endorsed by this amendment, and no same-identity incompatible runtime is permitted.

These clauses close result-bearing primitive/parser choices, not replace §§21.1–21.17. Named ports, DAG validation, immutable bindings, prohibited execution, limits and required identities remain as already specified. Unless expressly defaulted below, an omitted required argument is invalid; no coercion supplies it. The published registry must encode these rules exactly.

Remaining result-bearing argument/output closure: BYTE_COMPARE is exact length-and-byte equality of two byte inputs, with no ordering/operator default. ASSERT_MATCH asserts the same Boolean regex result as REGEX using actual/pattern/optional flags; ordered assertions use the exact ordering above. Each assertion yields only SATISFIED or VIOLATED on valid data, with other terminal dispositions propagated as D5 states. The optional message on assertions is a non-null string, absent by default, used only as diagnostic text and never to alter a result. SORT/UNIQUE require arrays and return arrays; MIN/MAX/SUM require arrays as stated. HASH_SHA256 requires bytes; REGEX requires string value/pattern; selectors require a string path and the defined structured value. Unknown optional arguments and implicit operand/binding selection are prohibited. Authoring shortcuts remain permitted only when they compile to the identical explicit §21.3 DAG and named ports. No extra primitive, alternate successful result type or undeclared default is authorized by registry publication. These additions close the result-bearing choices identified in the bounded argument/port omission comparison; the full generated registry still receives the independent §§2.2/14.5 review.

XML selectors start with exactly one slash, then child-element segments named [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]* or *, optionally followed by [positive safe integer]. The first segment matches the document element at position 1; later positions apply within each parent's matching child elements. Only the final segment may be @name or text(). Element results are arrays of the canonical element-node values defined in D4; attribute results are arrays of existing exact attribute strings; text() returns one string per selected element, concatenating descendant text/CDATA in document order and excluding comments. A wholly empty selection at any segment, including a final attribute selection, is UNDETERMINED. A selected element with no text yields the known empty string, not a missing selection. Other selector syntax is invalid before execution.

PARSE_XML supports the XML 1.0 UTF-8 subset with one root, scalar-valid XML characters, the element/attribute name grammar above, quoted unique attributes, matching tags, comments, CDATA, the five predefined entities and legal decimal/hex numeric character references. An optional initial declaration states version 1.0, optional encoding UTF-8 and optional standalone yes/no in that order. CRLF and CR normalize to LF; literal attribute tab/newline/CR normalize to spaces, while numeric character references preserve their referenced character. DTDs, custom entities, processing instructions, namespace expansion and unsupported declarations are not native semantics. Names containing a colon remain literal names, not namespace-resolved names. Comments do not enter text() output; CDATA does. Invalid/unsupported content cannot yield a successful partial parse.

Test IR is a topologically ordered directed acyclic graph. Every step has a unique application-validated stepId, one registered op, and an explicit inputs object. Each input references exactly one literal, immutable binding, or prior step output. A step may reference only an earlier step. Hidden accumulators, implicit stacks, ambient project state, ambient current values, operand-by-position rules, and implementation-dependent input selection are prohibited.

Every registered operation declares named input ports, output ports, exact types, cardinalities, deterministic error codes, error propagation, and resource-cost category. Each operation declares exact input arity and types and one normalized output type. Multi-artifact branches use explicit step references. BYTE_COMPARE and COMPARE receive explicit left and right inputs. Assertions receive explicit actual and expected inputs. A failed or unknown predecessor prevents dependent execution and propagates the registered terminal disposition without partial canonical result; errors propagate as typed execution failure and no later step may consume a failed output. Intermediate step outputs exist only for the current execution unless explicitly emitted as observations or evidence.
D. Insert after §21.17: residual native semantics
D4. Text, CSV, XML and regex.

Unsupported definition syntax, unknown arguments/operations and invalid declared types reject Stage 06 ingestion. Missing required material before execution is BLOCKED. Once started, invalid/unrepresentable data, no-match selection, empty required aggregate, numeric overflow or unsupported precision yields UNDETERMINED; runtime limit/platform/worker failure yields EXECUTION_FAILED. A dependency cannot consume an error or partial output. The operation registry declares deterministic typed codes for these categories; wording is not a new semantic contract. Apply §21.16 to every affected language/parser/selector/operation identity. No existing digest is endorsed by this amendment, and no same-identity incompatible runtime is permitted.

These clauses close result-bearing primitive/parser choices, not replace §§21.1–21.17. Named ports, DAG validation, immutable bindings, prohibited execution, limits and required identities remain as already specified. Unless expressly defaulted below, an omitted required argument is invalid; no coercion supplies it. The published registry must encode these rules exactly.

Remaining result-bearing argument/output closure: BYTE_COMPARE is exact length-and-byte equality of two byte inputs, with no ordering/operator default. ASSERT_MATCH asserts the same Boolean regex result as REGEX using actual/pattern/optional flags; ordered assertions use the exact ordering above. Each assertion yields only SATISFIED or VIOLATED on valid data, with other terminal dispositions propagated as D5 states. The optional message on assertions is a non-null string, absent by default, used only as diagnostic text and never to alter a result. SORT/UNIQUE require arrays and return arrays; MIN/MAX/SUM require arrays as stated. HASH_SHA256 requires bytes; REGEX requires string value/pattern; selectors require a string path and the defined structured value. Unknown optional arguments and implicit operand/binding selection are prohibited. Authoring shortcuts remain permitted only when they compile to the identical explicit §21.3 DAG and named ports. No extra primitive, alternate successful result type or undeclared default is authorized by registry publication. These additions close the result-bearing choices identified in the bounded argument/port omission comparison; the full generated registry still receives the independent §§2.2/14.5 review.

A failed or unknown predecessor prevents dependent execution and propagates the registered terminal disposition without partial canonical result; errors propagate as typed execution failure and no later step may consume a failed output. Intermediate step outputs exist only for the current execution unless explicitly emitted as observations or evidence.

Test IR is a topologically ordered directed acyclic graph. Every step has a unique application-validated stepId, one registered op, and an explicit inputs object. Each input references exactly one literal, immutable binding, or prior step output. A step may reference only an earlier step. Hidden accumulators, implicit stacks, ambient project state, ambient current values, operand-by-position rules, and implementation-dependent input selection are prohibited.

Every registered operation declares named input ports, output ports, exact types, cardinalities, deterministic error codes, error propagation, and resource-cost category. Each operation declares exact input arity and types and one normalized output type. Multi-artifact branches use explicit step references. BYTE_COMPARE and COMPARE receive explicit left and right inputs. Assertions receive explicit actual and expected inputs. A failed or unknown predecessor prevents dependent execution and propagates the registered terminal disposition without partial canonical result; errors propagate as typed execution failure and no later step may consume a failed output. Intermediate step outputs exist only for the current execution unless explicitly emitted as observations or evidence.
D. Insert after §21.17: residual native semantics
D4. Text, CSV, XML and regex.

Unsupported definition syntax, unknown arguments/operations and invalid declared types reject Stage 06 ingestion. Missing required material before execution is BLOCKED. Once started, invalid/unrepresentable data, no-match selection, empty required aggregate, numeric overflow or unsupported precision yields UNDETERMINED; runtime limit/platform/worker failure yields EXECUTION_FAILED. A dependency cannot consume an error or partial output. The operation registry declares deterministic typed codes for these categories; wording is not a new semantic contract. Apply §21.16 to every affected language/parser/selector/operation identity. No existing digest is endorsed by this amendment, and no same-identity incompatible runtime is permitted.

These clauses close result-bearing primitive/parser choices, not replace §§21.1–21.17. Named ports, DAG validation, immutable bindings, prohibited execution, limits and required identities remain as already specified. Unless expressly defaulted below, an omitted required argument is invalid; no coercion supplies it. The published registry must encode these rules exactly.

statement: SORT/UNIQUE require arrays and return arrays

Test IR is a topologically ordered directed acyclic graph. Every step has a unique application-validated stepId, one registered op, and an explicit inputs object. Each input references exactly one literal, immutable binding, or prior step output. A step may reference only an earlier step. Hidden accumulators, implicit stacks, ambient project state, ambient current values, operand-by-position rules, and implementation-dependent input selection are prohibited.

Every registered operation declares named input ports, output ports, exact types, cardinalities, deterministic error codes, error propagation, and resource-cost category. Each operation declares exact input arity and types and one normalized output type. Multi-artifact branches use explicit step references. BYTE_COMPARE and COMPARE receive explicit left and right inputs. Assertions receive explicit actual and expected inputs. A failed or unknown predecessor prevents dependent execution and propagates the registered terminal disposition without partial canonical result; errors propagate as typed execution failure and no later step may consume a failed output. Intermediate step outputs exist only for the current execution unless explicitly emitted as observations or evidence.
D. Insert after §21.17: residual native semantics
D5. Errors and identity.

These clauses close result-bearing primitive/parser choices, not replace §§21.1–21.17. Named ports, DAG validation, immutable bindings, prohibited execution, limits and required identities remain as already specified. Unless expressly defaulted below, an omitted required argument is invalid; no coercion supplies it. The published registry must encode these rules exactly.

Remaining result-bearing argument/output closure: BYTE_COMPARE is exact length-and-byte equality of two byte inputs, with no ordering/operator default. ASSERT_MATCH asserts the same Boolean regex result as REGEX using actual/pattern/optional flags; ordered assertions use the exact ordering above. Each assertion yields only SATISFIED or VIOLATED on valid data, with other terminal dispositions propagated as D5 states. The optional message on assertions is a non-null string, absent by default, used only as diagnostic text and never to alter a result. SORT/UNIQUE require arrays and return arrays; MIN/MAX/SUM require arrays as stated. HASH_SHA256 requires bytes; REGEX requires string value/pattern; selectors require a string path and the defined structured value. Unknown optional arguments and implicit operand/binding selection are prohibited. Authoring shortcuts remain permitted only when they compile to the identical explicit §21.3 DAG and named ports. No extra primitive, alternate successful result type or undeclared default is authorized by registry publication. These additions close the result-bearing choices identified in the bounded argument/port omission comparison; the full generated registry still receives the independent §§2.2/14.5 review.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText:
No other stage-operation combination is valid. The registry declares for each listed operation its allowed response types, target-slot derivation, required input families, writable fields and collections, reservation requirement, independence requirement, completion predicate, retry behavior, and whether it is agent, human, or application executed.

Operation execution and response permissions are closed:

- External-agent operations are COMPLETE at Stages 01-09, 15, 21, 23, 24, 25, and 26; SEMANTIC_CHALLENGE; RECONCILE_INTAKE; SEARCH_ADEQUACY_REVIEW; RECONCILE_SOURCE_SEARCH; RECONCILE_RESEARCH; DISPOSITION_CHALLENGE; ATOMICITY_CHALLENGE; RECONCILE_REQUIREMENTS; SEMANTIC_REVIEW; RECONCILE_REQUIREMENT_SET; PROOF_REVIEW; RECONCILE_VERIFICATION_SUITE; EXECUTE_RUN; VERIFY; COMPARE; ROOT_CAUSE; REGRESSION; CORRECT; RECONCILE at Stage 26; ADVISORY_REVIEW at Stage 27; EXECUTE_EXTERNAL_TEST; INVESTIGATE_MISSING_EVIDENCE; and EXECUTE_FAILURE_TEST, EXECUTE_REGRESSION, and REGRESSION_VERIFY when externally routed. They require an operation reservation and file-first package. Their responseType is exactly DATA_PROPOSAL, HUMAN_INPUT_REQUIRED, BLOCKED, or EXECUTION_FAILED as permitted by the operation's field contract. ADVISORY_REVIEW at Stage 27 is optional and non-gating: it writes releaseGateReviews records only and cannot modify, delay, or substitute for any CALCULATE_RELEASE input, calculation, or state.
- Application commands are EXECUTE_FAILURE_TEST when natively routed, EXECUTE_REGRESSION when natively routed, REGRESSION_VERIFY when natively routed, FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, COMPLETE at Stage 18, CONFIRM at Stage 19, FREEZE_BASELINE, RUN_NATIVE_TESTS, RUN_NATIVE_ATTACKS, FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE, VERIFY_IDENTITY, CALCULATE_RELEASE, CALCULATE_EVIDENCE_CHAINS, and CALCULATE_TERMINAL. They accept no external response envelope and commit only application-owned results through the universal command path. COMPLETE at Stage 18 and CONFIRM at Stage 19 are application-calculated convergence and confirmation determinations; agents contribute only the separately declared explanatory fields of the owning record families. FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, FREEZE_BASELINE, and FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE consume and reference the required current humanDecisions records; they never create human authority.
- HUMAN_DECISION commands are CAPTURE_DELIVERY_INTENT; application confirmation of a newly reported human-origin answer; and RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION, one global application-validated command bound to exactly one registered purpose and target per invocation. The closed RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION purpose enum is INTENT_CONFIRMATION, CANDIDATE_COMPONENT_SELECTION, BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, DISCLOSURE_AUTHORIZATION, EXTERNAL_ACTION_RISK_AUTHORIZATION, CONTROLLED_EXCEPTION, REGRESSION_RETIREMENT_AUTHORIZATION, BACKUP_POLICY_SELECTION, TRADEOFF_OR_SCOPE_DECISION, VISUAL_BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, and HUMAN_AUTHORITY_CORRECTION. Each purpose writes only the humanDecisions record and the human-decision-owned fields FIELD_REGISTRY declares for that purpose and target. HUMAN commands are SAVE_HUMAN_INPUT, which creates and edits User Job Input and saves Section 18 fallback answers with their declared consequences, and RECORD_HUMAN_OBSERVATION, which records human-owned observation and evidence records for human-inspection routes. These commands write only their declared HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION fields and records, accept no agent-owned canonical fields, and accept no external response envelope.
- EXPORT_PROMPT_FILE, EXPORT_EXECUTION_PACKAGE, SELECT_RESPONSE_JSON_FILE, SELECT_RETURNED_FILES, EXPORT_OR_SHARE_AUTHORIZED_ARTIFACTS, and RECORD_DELIVERY_EVIDENCE are operator actions. They create only the application receipts and human or external evidence explicitly declared by their contracts.

For every operation, TARGET_SLOT = SHA-256(closed-loop-canonical-json/1 of contractProfileId, jobId, stage, operation, and all operation-specific target identities required by Section 14.7). The target slot excludes projectRevision so an exact retry retains its slot; expectedRevision and scopeHash remain separate mandatory preconditions. No operation can write a family or field not listed in its FIELD_REGISTRY entry.

26.6 Dimensioned independence

Independence is recorded separately for APPLICATION_SESSION_DISTINCTNESS, APPLICATION_INPUT_ISOLATION, USER_TRANSFER_CONFORMITY, EXTERNAL_CONTEXT_IDENTIFIER_DISTINCTNESS, PROVIDER_CONTEXT_INDEPENDENCE, EXECUTOR_OR_REVIEWER_ROLE_SEPARATION, and ENVIRONMENT_INDEPENDENCE where required. APPLICATION_ESTABLISHED means only that application-observable dimensions required by the contract are satisfied. Distinct IDs do not prove hidden provider-state independence. A required UNKNOWN dimension blocks or leaves the result undetermined.

Every external operation contract declares MINIMUM_INPUT_BINDING_BASIS from APPLICATION_OBSERVED, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL, EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED, and SELF_ASSERTED. An echoed manifest identity and per-member digests establish at most EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED. SELF_ASSERTED or UNKNOWN cannot satisfy an operation whose contract requires byte-exact input possession, and gates derive admissibility from the recorded basis.

29.12 Universal proposition state and three-valued logic

Every release-bearing proposition, applicability condition, independence condition, entailment conclusion, source-authenticity conclusion, environment claim, and external-capability claim carries truthValue TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN; epistemicBasis APPLICATION_OBSERVED, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL, EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED, SELF_ASSERTED, or NONE; currentScopeStatus CURRENT or STALE; freshnessStatus CURRENT, EXPIRED, UNKNOWN, or NOT_APPLICABLE; contradictionStatus CLEAR or CONTRADICTED; reasons; supportingEvidenceIds; and a derivation or accepted semantic-review identity.

TRUE requires affirmative support meeting the proof obligation. FALSE requires sufficient current evidence establishing noncompliance or negation. UNKNOWN applies when neither is established and fails closed wherever affirmative proof is required. Missing data is UNKNOWN unless a closed-universe rule affirmatively establishes FALSE. Contradictory sufficient evidence blocks and is never averaged away.

29.13 Proposition and proof-expression contract

Every normative requirement has one primary PROPOSITION_ID. Independent truth conditions are split or represented by one accepted acyclic proof expression. Semantic sameness is established only by an independent EQUIVALENT review; wording, embeddings, filenames, and hashes cannot merge propositions.

The closed proof-expression language permits LEAF, ALL_OF, ANY_OF, and AT_LEAST_K only. It has no arbitrary code, unrestricted negation, implicit coercion, stale references, or empty operators. ALL_OF is TRUE when all children are TRUE, FALSE when any is FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. ANY_OF is TRUE when any is TRUE, FALSE when all are FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. AT_LEAST_K is TRUE when trueCount ≥ K, FALSE when trueCount + unknownCount < K, and UNKNOWN otherwise.

Every current applicable release-bearing proposition has exactly one current PROOF_OBLIGATION_ID identifying its proof expression, required leaves, evidence classes, allowed epistemic bases, artifacts, dependencies, freshness, independence, verification timing, current satisfaction, blockers, and scope hash. Optional, advisory, stale, historical, or unregistered results cannot satisfy it.

EQUIVALENT applies only to proposition-to-proposition sameness. The relation between a test and a proof leaf, and between a proof expression and its proposition, is sufficiency, established by the accepted Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW. A LEAF references exactly one of: a canonical test with its required disposition, an observation-backed proposition, an applicability or activation condition, or a prerequisite proof obligation; each leaf declares its truth extraction, required evidence classes, and scope binding, and no other leaf target is valid in version 1. An ANY_OF expression is accepted only when the review establishes that each branch alone suffices to establish the parent proposition; an AT_LEAST_K expression is accepted only when every permitted K-combination suffices or an explicitly reviewed combinatorial sufficiency contract covers it. A branch that weakens proof strength is rejected at Stage 06.

29.14 Observation, entailment, origin, and freshness

Every release-bearing evidence path is EVIDENCE_RECORD → OBSERVATION_RECORD → proposition or proof leaf. An observation identifies exact subject, location or measurement point, finding, method/tool, inputs and outputs, hashes, origin, submitting actor, epistemic basis, time/freshness fields, source evidence, scope, and raw-response or native-execution provenance.

Every observation has an accepted relation ESTABLISHES, REFUTES, SUPPORTS_ONLY, CONTEXT_ONLY, DOES_NOT_ADDRESS, or UNKNOWN. Only ESTABLISHES provides affirmative proof; REFUTES provides failure evidence; SUPPORTS_ONLY and CONTEXT_ONLY cannot independently satisfy a proof obligation. Normalization never elevates an external claim.

Time-sensitive evidence records observedAt, its DEVICE_REPORTED, SOURCE_ASSERTED, or VERIFIED_EXTERNAL basis, validFrom, validUntil, supersession, freshness requirement, status, and reason. Required freshness that cannot be established is UNKNOWN. Current justificatory evidence is acyclic.

VERIFIED_EXTERNAL is achieved only under a registered attestation-verification contract fixing the evidence type, the attesting tool or system identity, the verification method, the bound inputs including the operation challengeNonce or reservation, the freshness rule, and the failure semantics. Absent such a registered contract, the basis remains EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED or weaker.
F2. Insert after §26.6: closed-loop-external-input-binding-minima/1
MINIMUM_INPUT_BINDING_BASIS is EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED for the external route of each pair in the following closed mapping:

The mapping has 88 external routes: 50 from the original §14.6 list plus 23 later failure-test and 15 later regression routes. F1's closed lists, not a wildcard allowing arbitrary operation names or stages, determine the additional pairs. The minimum does not grant operation availability or new writer authority. ADVISORY_REVIEW remains optional and non-gating.

For an external route, exact attributable echoes of the application-issued package/manifest identity and each required member identity/digest may establish EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED under the existing input-binding contract; missing or mismatched echoes cannot. A package download, filename, provider label or unbound assertion is insufficient. Echoes never become APPLICATION_OBSERVED external possession, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL attestation, or proof of hidden provider independence. Recording that the application supplied bytes does not prove that an external recipient independently possessed or executed them.

If the applicable proof obligation, evidence contract or dimensioned-independence contract requires a stronger or distinct basis, that requirement also must be met. This generic minimum cannot weaken it, convert SUPPORTS_ONLY into ESTABLISHES, remove a required accepted review, waive unknown freshness/independence, or supply a successful result. §29.14's registered attestation-verification contract remains necessary for VERIFIED_EXTERNAL. Actual basis and its supporting observations remain recorded and evaluated by the existing gates.

TRUE requires affirmative support meeting the proof obligation. FALSE requires sufficient current evidence establishing noncompliance or negation. UNKNOWN applies when neither is established and fails closed wherever affirmative proof is required. Missing data is UNKNOWN unless a closed-universe rule affirmatively establishes FALSE. Contradictory sufficient evidence blocks and is never averaged away.

29.13 Proposition and proof-expression contract

Every normative requirement has one primary PROPOSITION_ID. Independent truth conditions are split or represented by one accepted acyclic proof expression. Semantic sameness is established only by an independent EQUIVALENT review; wording, embeddings, filenames, and hashes cannot merge propositions.

The closed proof-expression language permits LEAF, ALL_OF, ANY_OF, and AT_LEAST_K only. It has no arbitrary code, unrestricted negation, implicit coercion, stale references, or empty operators. ALL_OF is TRUE when all children are TRUE, FALSE when any is FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. ANY_OF is TRUE when any is TRUE, FALSE when all are FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. AT_LEAST_K is TRUE when trueCount ≥ K, FALSE when trueCount + unknownCount < K, and UNKNOWN otherwise.

Every current applicable release-bearing proposition has exactly one current PROOF_OBLIGATION_ID identifying its proof expression, required leaves, evidence classes, allowed epistemic bases, artifacts, dependencies, freshness, independence, verification timing, current satisfaction, blockers, and scope hash. Optional, advisory, stale, historical, or unregistered results cannot satisfy it.

EQUIVALENT applies only to proposition-to-proposition sameness. The relation between a test and a proof leaf, and between a proof expression and its proposition, is sufficiency, established by the accepted Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW. A LEAF references exactly one of: a canonical test with its required disposition, an observation-backed proposition, an applicability or activation condition, or a prerequisite proof obligation; each leaf declares its truth extraction, required evidence classes, and scope binding, and no other leaf target is valid in version 1. An ANY_OF expression is accepted only when the review establishes that each branch alone suffices to establish the parent proposition; an AT_LEAST_K expression is accepted only when every permitted K-combination suffices or an explicitly reviewed combinatorial sufficiency contract covers it. A branch that weakens proof strength is rejected at Stage 06.

Every release-bearing evidence path is EVIDENCE_RECORD → OBSERVATION_RECORD → proposition or proof leaf. An observation identifies exact subject, location or measurement point, finding, method/tool, inputs and outputs, hashes, origin, submitting actor, epistemic basis, time/freshness fields, source evidence, scope, and raw-response or native-execution provenance.

Every observation has an accepted relation ESTABLISHES, REFUTES, SUPPORTS_ONLY, CONTEXT_ONLY, DOES_NOT_ADDRESS, or UNKNOWN. Only ESTABLISHES provides affirmative proof; REFUTES provides failure evidence; SUPPORTS_ONLY and CONTEXT_ONLY cannot independently satisfy a proof obligation. Normalization never elevates an external claim.

Time-sensitive evidence records observedAt, its DEVICE_REPORTED, SOURCE_ASSERTED, or VERIFIED_EXTERNAL basis, validFrom, validUntil, supersession, freshness requirement, status, and reason. Required freshness that cannot be established is UNKNOWN. Current justificatory evidence is acyclic.

VERIFIED_EXTERNAL is achieved only under a registered attestation-verification contract fixing the evidence type, the attesting tool or system identity, the verification method, the bound inputs including the operation challengeNonce or reservation, the freshness rule, and the failure semantics. APPLICATION_ESTABLISHED means only that application-observable dimensions required by the contract are satisfied. Distinct IDs do not prove hidden provider-state independence. A required UNKNOWN dimension blocks or leaves the result undetermined.

Every external operation contract declares MINIMUM_INPUT_BINDING_BASIS from APPLICATION_OBSERVED, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL, EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED, and SELF_ASSERTED. An echoed manifest identity and per-member digests establish at most EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED. SELF_ASSERTED or UNKNOWN cannot satisfy an operation whose contract requires byte-exact input possession, and gates derive admissibility from the recorded basis.

29.12 Universal proposition state and three-valued logic

Every release-bearing proposition, applicability condition, independence condition, entailment conclusion, source-authenticity conclusion, environment claim, and external-capability claim carries truthValue TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN; epistemicBasis APPLICATION_OBSERVED, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL, EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED, SELF_ASSERTED, or NONE; currentScopeStatus CURRENT or STALE; freshnessStatus CURRENT, EXPIRED, UNKNOWN, or NOT_APPLICABLE; contradictionStatus CLEAR or CONTRADICTED; reasons; supportingEvidenceIds; and a derivation or accepted semantic-review identity.

TRUE requires affirmative support meeting the proof obligation. FALSE requires sufficient current evidence establishing noncompliance or negation. UNKNOWN applies when neither is established and fails closed wherever affirmative proof is required. Missing data is UNKNOWN unless a closed-universe rule affirmatively establishes FALSE. Contradictory sufficient evidence blocks and is never averaged away.

29.13 Proposition and proof-expression contract

Every normative requirement has one primary PROPOSITION_ID. Independent truth conditions are split or represented by one accepted acyclic proof expression. Semantic sameness is established only by an independent EQUIVALENT review; wording, embeddings, filenames, and hashes cannot merge propositions.

The closed proof-expression language permits LEAF, ALL_OF, ANY_OF, and AT_LEAST_K only. It has no arbitrary code, unrestricted negation, implicit coercion, stale references, or empty operators. ALL_OF is TRUE when all children are TRUE, FALSE when any is FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. ANY_OF is TRUE when any is TRUE, FALSE when all are FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. AT_LEAST_K is TRUE when trueCount ≥ K, FALSE when trueCount + unknownCount < K, and UNKNOWN otherwise.

Every current applicable release-bearing proposition has exactly one current PROOF_OBLIGATION_ID identifying its proof expression, required leaves, evidence classes, allowed epistemic bases, artifacts, dependencies, freshness, independence, verification timing, current satisfaction, blockers, and scope hash. Optional, advisory, stale, historical, or unregistered results cannot satisfy it.

EQUIVALENT applies only to proposition-to-proposition sameness. The relation between a test and a proof leaf, and between a proof expression and its proposition, is sufficiency, established by the accepted Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW. A LEAF references exactly one of: a canonical test with its required disposition, an observation-backed proposition, an applicability or activation condition, or a prerequisite proof obligation; each leaf declares its truth extraction, required evidence classes, and scope binding, and no other leaf target is valid in version 1. An ANY_OF expression is accepted only when the review establishes that each branch alone suffices to establish the parent proposition; an AT_LEAST_K expression is accepted only when every permitted K-combination suffices or an explicitly reviewed combinatorial sufficiency contract covers it. A branch that weakens proof strength is rejected at Stage 06.

29.14 Observation, entailment, origin, and freshness

Every release-bearing evidence path is EVIDENCE_RECORD → OBSERVATION_RECORD → proposition or proof leaf. An observation identifies exact subject, location or measurement point, finding, method/tool, inputs and outputs, hashes, origin, submitting actor, epistemic basis, time/freshness fields, source evidence, scope, and raw-response or native-execution provenance.

Every observation has an accepted relation ESTABLISHES, REFUTES, SUPPORTS_ONLY, CONTEXT_ONLY, DOES_NOT_ADDRESS, or UNKNOWN. Only ESTABLISHES provides affirmative proof; REFUTES provides failure evidence; SUPPORTS_ONLY and CONTEXT_ONLY cannot independently satisfy a proof obligation. Normalization never elevates an external claim.

Time-sensitive evidence records observedAt, its DEVICE_REPORTED, SOURCE_ASSERTED, or VERIFIED_EXTERNAL basis, validFrom, validUntil, supersession, freshness requirement, status, and reason. Required freshness that cannot be established is UNKNOWN. Current justificatory evidence is acyclic.

VERIFIED_EXTERNAL is achieved only under a registered attestation-verification contract fixing the evidence type, the attesting tool or system identity, the verification method, the bound inputs including the operation challengeNonce or reservation, the freshness rule, and the failure semantics. contextSourceLocations.controllingText:
No other stage-operation combination is valid. The registry declares for each listed operation its allowed response types, target-slot derivation, required input families, writable fields and collections, reservation requirement, independence requirement, completion predicate, retry behavior, and whether it is agent, human, or application executed.

Operation execution and response permissions are closed:

- External-agent operations are COMPLETE at Stages 01-09, 15, 21, 23, 24, 25, and 26; SEMANTIC_CHALLENGE; RECONCILE_INTAKE; SEARCH_ADEQUACY_REVIEW; RECONCILE_SOURCE_SEARCH; RECONCILE_RESEARCH; DISPOSITION_CHALLENGE; ATOMICITY_CHALLENGE; RECONCILE_REQUIREMENTS; SEMANTIC_REVIEW; RECONCILE_REQUIREMENT_SET; PROOF_REVIEW; RECONCILE_VERIFICATION_SUITE; EXECUTE_RUN; VERIFY; COMPARE; ROOT_CAUSE; REGRESSION; CORRECT; RECONCILE at Stage 26; ADVISORY_REVIEW at Stage 27; EXECUTE_EXTERNAL_TEST; INVESTIGATE_MISSING_EVIDENCE; and EXECUTE_FAILURE_TEST, EXECUTE_REGRESSION, and REGRESSION_VERIFY when externally routed. They require an operation reservation and file-first package. Their responseType is exactly DATA_PROPOSAL, HUMAN_INPUT_REQUIRED, BLOCKED, or EXECUTION_FAILED as permitted by the operation's field contract. ADVISORY_REVIEW at Stage 27 is optional and non-gating: it writes releaseGateReviews records only and cannot modify, delay, or substitute for any CALCULATE_RELEASE input, calculation, or state.
- Application commands are EXECUTE_FAILURE_TEST when natively routed, EXECUTE_REGRESSION when natively routed, REGRESSION_VERIFY when natively routed, FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, COMPLETE at Stage 18, CONFIRM at Stage 19, FREEZE_BASELINE, RUN_NATIVE_TESTS, RUN_NATIVE_ATTACKS, FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE, VERIFY_IDENTITY, CALCULATE_RELEASE, CALCULATE_EVIDENCE_CHAINS, and CALCULATE_TERMINAL. They accept no external response envelope and commit only application-owned results through the universal command path. COMPLETE at Stage 18 and CONFIRM at Stage 19 are application-calculated convergence and confirmation determinations; agents contribute only the separately declared explanatory fields of the owning record families. FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, FREEZE_BASELINE, and FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE consume and reference the required current humanDecisions records; they never create human authority.
- HUMAN_DECISION commands are CAPTURE_DELIVERY_INTENT; application confirmation of a newly reported human-origin answer; and RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION, one global application-validated command bound to exactly one registered purpose and target per invocation. The closed RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION purpose enum is INTENT_CONFIRMATION, CANDIDATE_COMPONENT_SELECTION, BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, DISCLOSURE_AUTHORIZATION, EXTERNAL_ACTION_RISK_AUTHORIZATION, CONTROLLED_EXCEPTION, REGRESSION_RETIREMENT_AUTHORIZATION, BACKUP_POLICY_SELECTION, TRADEOFF_OR_SCOPE_DECISION, VISUAL_BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, and HUMAN_AUTHORITY_CORRECTION. Each purpose writes only the humanDecisions record and the human-decision-owned fields FIELD_REGISTRY declares for that purpose and target. HUMAN commands are SAVE_HUMAN_INPUT, which creates and edits User Job Input and saves Section 18 fallback answers with their declared consequences, and RECORD_HUMAN_OBSERVATION, which records human-owned observation and evidence records for human-inspection routes. These commands write only their declared HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION fields and records, accept no agent-owned canonical fields, and accept no external response envelope.
- EXPORT_PROMPT_FILE, EXPORT_EXECUTION_PACKAGE, SELECT_RESPONSE_JSON_FILE, SELECT_RETURNED_FILES, EXPORT_OR_SHARE_AUTHORIZED_ARTIFACTS, and RECORD_DELIVERY_EVIDENCE are operator actions. They create only the application receipts and human or external evidence explicitly declared by their contracts.

For every operation, TARGET_SLOT = SHA-256(closed-loop-canonical-json/1 of contractProfileId, jobId, stage, operation, and all operation-specific target identities required by Section 14.7). The target slot excludes projectRevision so an exact retry retains its slot; expectedRevision and scopeHash remain separate mandatory preconditions. No operation can write a family or field not listed in its FIELD_REGISTRY entry.

26.6 Dimensioned independence

Independence is recorded separately for APPLICATION_SESSION_DISTINCTNESS, APPLICATION_INPUT_ISOLATION, USER_TRANSFER_CONFORMITY, EXTERNAL_CONTEXT_IDENTIFIER_DISTINCTNESS, PROVIDER_CONTEXT_INDEPENDENCE, EXECUTOR_OR_REVIEWER_ROLE_SEPARATION, and ENVIRONMENT_INDEPENDENCE where required. APPLICATION_ESTABLISHED means only that application-observable dimensions required by the contract are satisfied. Distinct IDs do not prove hidden provider-state independence. A required UNKNOWN dimension blocks or leaves the result undetermined.

Every external operation contract declares MINIMUM_INPUT_BINDING_BASIS from APPLICATION_OBSERVED, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL, EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED, and SELF_ASSERTED. An echoed manifest identity and per-member digests establish at most EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED. SELF_ASSERTED or UNKNOWN cannot satisfy an operation whose contract requires byte-exact input possession, and gates derive admissibility from the recorded basis.

29.12 Universal proposition state and three-valued logic

Every release-bearing proposition, applicability condition, independence condition, entailment conclusion, source-authenticity conclusion, environment claim, and external-capability claim carries truthValue TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN; epistemicBasis APPLICATION_OBSERVED, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL, EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED, SELF_ASSERTED, or NONE; currentScopeStatus CURRENT or STALE; freshnessStatus CURRENT, EXPIRED, UNKNOWN, or NOT_APPLICABLE; contradictionStatus CLEAR or CONTRADICTED; reasons; supportingEvidenceIds; and a derivation or accepted semantic-review identity.

TRUE requires affirmative support meeting the proof obligation. FALSE requires sufficient current evidence establishing noncompliance or negation. UNKNOWN applies when neither is established and fails closed wherever affirmative proof is required. Missing data is UNKNOWN unless a closed-universe rule affirmatively establishes FALSE. Contradictory sufficient evidence blocks and is never averaged away.

29.13 Proposition and proof-expression contract

Every normative requirement has one primary PROPOSITION_ID. Independent truth conditions are split or represented by one accepted acyclic proof expression. Semantic sameness is established only by an independent EQUIVALENT review; wording, embeddings, filenames, and hashes cannot merge propositions.

The closed proof-expression language permits LEAF, ALL_OF, ANY_OF, and AT_LEAST_K only. It has no arbitrary code, unrestricted negation, implicit coercion, stale references, or empty operators. ALL_OF is TRUE when all children are TRUE, FALSE when any is FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. ANY_OF is TRUE when any is TRUE, FALSE when all are FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. AT_LEAST_K is TRUE when trueCount ≥ K, FALSE when trueCount + unknownCount < K, and UNKNOWN otherwise.

Every current applicable release-bearing proposition has exactly one current PROOF_OBLIGATION_ID identifying its proof expression, required leaves, evidence classes, allowed epistemic bases, artifacts, dependencies, freshness, independence, verification timing, current satisfaction, blockers, and scope hash. Optional, advisory, stale, historical, or unregistered results cannot satisfy it.

EQUIVALENT applies only to proposition-to-proposition sameness. The relation between a test and a proof leaf, and between a proof expression and its proposition, is sufficiency, established by the accepted Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW. A LEAF references exactly one of: a canonical test with its required disposition, an observation-backed proposition, an applicability or activation condition, or a prerequisite proof obligation; each leaf declares its truth extraction, required evidence classes, and scope binding, and no other leaf target is valid in version 1. An ANY_OF expression is accepted only when the review establishes that each branch alone suffices to establish the parent proposition; an AT_LEAST_K expression is accepted only when every permitted K-combination suffices or an explicitly reviewed combinatorial sufficiency contract covers it. A branch that weakens proof strength is rejected at Stage 06.

29.14 Observation, entailment, origin, and freshness

Every release-bearing evidence path is EVIDENCE_RECORD → OBSERVATION_RECORD → proposition or proof leaf. An observation identifies exact subject, location or measurement point, finding, method/tool, inputs and outputs, hashes, origin, submitting actor, epistemic basis, time/freshness fields, source evidence, scope, and raw-response or native-execution provenance.

Every observation has an accepted relation ESTABLISHES, REFUTES, SUPPORTS_ONLY, CONTEXT_ONLY, DOES_NOT_ADDRESS, or UNKNOWN. Only ESTABLISHES provides affirmative proof; REFUTES provides failure evidence; SUPPORTS_ONLY and CONTEXT_ONLY cannot independently satisfy a proof obligation. Normalization never elevates an external claim.

Time-sensitive evidence records observedAt, its DEVICE_REPORTED, SOURCE_ASSERTED, or VERIFIED_EXTERNAL basis, validFrom, validUntil, supersession, freshness requirement, status, and reason. Required freshness that cannot be established is UNKNOWN. Current justificatory evidence is acyclic.

VERIFIED_EXTERNAL is achieved only under a registered attestation-verification contract fixing the evidence type, the attesting tool or system identity, the verification method, the bound inputs including the operation challengeNonce or reservation, the freshness rule, and the failure semantics. Absent such a registered contract, the basis remains EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED or weaker.
F2. Insert after §26.6: closed-loop-external-input-binding-minima/1
MINIMUM_INPUT_BINDING_BASIS is EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED for the external route of each pair in the following closed mapping:

The mapping has 88 external routes: 50 from the original §14.6 list plus 23 later failure-test and 15 later regression routes. F1's closed lists, not a wildcard allowing arbitrary operation names or stages, determine the additional pairs. The minimum does not grant operation availability or new writer authority. ADVISORY_REVIEW remains optional and non-gating.

For an external route, exact attributable echoes of the application-issued package/manifest identity and each required member identity/digest may establish EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED under the existing input-binding contract; missing or mismatched echoes cannot. A package download, filename, provider label or unbound assertion is insufficient. Echoes never become APPLICATION_OBSERVED external possession, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL attestation, or proof of hidden provider independence. Recording that the application supplied bytes does not prove that an external recipient independently possessed or executed them.

If the applicable proof obligation, evidence contract or dimensioned-independence contract requires a stronger or distinct basis, that requirement also must be met. This generic minimum cannot weaken it, convert SUPPORTS_ONLY into ESTABLISHES, remove a required accepted review, waive unknown freshness/independence, or supply a successful result. §29.14's registered attestation-verification contract remains necessary for VERIFIED_EXTERNAL. Actual basis and its supporting observations remain recorded and evaluated by the existing gates.

Semantic sameness is established only by an independent EQUIVALENT review; wording, embeddings, filenames, and hashes cannot merge propositions.

The closed proof-expression language permits LEAF, ALL_OF, ANY_OF, and AT_LEAST_K only. It has no arbitrary code, unrestricted negation, implicit coercion, stale references, or empty operators. AT_LEAST_K is TRUE when trueCount ≥ K, FALSE when trueCount + unknownCount < K, and UNKNOWN otherwise.

Every current applicable release-bearing proposition has exactly one current PROOF_OBLIGATION_ID identifying its proof expression, required leaves, evidence classes, allowed epistemic bases, artifacts, dependencies, freshness, independence, verification timing, current satisfaction, blockers, and scope hash. Optional, advisory, stale, historical, or unregistered results cannot satisfy it.

EQUIVALENT applies only to proposition-to-proposition sameness. The relation between a test and a proof leaf, and between a proof expression and its proposition, is sufficiency, established by the accepted Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW. A LEAF references exactly one of: a canonical test with its required disposition, an observation-backed proposition, an applicability or activation condition, or a prerequisite proof obligation; each leaf declares its truth extraction, required evidence classes, and scope binding, and no other leaf target is valid in version 1. An ANY_OF expression is accepted only when the review establishes that each branch alone suffices to establish the parent proposition; an AT_LEAST_K expression is accepted only when every permitted K-combination suffices or an explicitly reviewed combinatorial sufficiency contract covers it. Every release-bearing evidence path is EVIDENCE_RECORD → OBSERVATION_RECORD → proposition or proof leaf. Every observation has an accepted relation ESTABLISHES, REFUTES, SUPPORTS_ONLY, CONTEXT_ONLY, DOES_NOT_ADDRESS, or UNKNOWN. Only ESTABLISHES provides affirmative proof; REFUTES provides failure evidence; SUPPORTS_ONLY and CONTEXT_ONLY cannot independently satisfy a proof obligation. VERIFIED_EXTERNAL is achieved only under a registered attestation-verification contract fixing the evidence type, the attesting tool or system identity, the verification method, the bound inputs including the operation challengeNonce or reservation, the freshness rule, and the failure semantics. 26.6 Dimensioned independence

29.12 Universal proposition state and three-valued logic

Every release-bearing proposition, applicability condition, independence condition, entailment conclusion, source-authenticity conclusion, environment claim, and external-capability claim carries truthValue TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN; epistemicBasis APPLICATION_OBSERVED, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL, EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED, SELF_ASSERTED, or NONE; currentScopeStatus CURRENT or STALE; freshnessStatus CURRENT, EXPIRED, UNKNOWN, or NOT_APPLICABLE; contradictionStatus CLEAR or CONTRADICTED; reasons; supportingEvidenceIds; and a derivation or accepted semantic-review identity.

TRUE requires affirmative support meeting the proof obligation. FALSE requires sufficient current evidence establishing noncompliance or negation. UNKNOWN applies when neither is established and fails closed wherever affirmative proof is required. Missing data is UNKNOWN unless a closed-universe rule affirmatively establishes FALSE. 29.13 Proposition and proof-expression contract

Every normative requirement has one primary PROPOSITION_ID. Independent truth conditions are split or represented by one accepted acyclic proof expression. The relation between a test and a proof leaf, and between a proof expression and its proposition, is sufficiency, established by the accepted Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW. An ANY_OF expression is accepted only when the review establishes that each branch alone suffices to establish the parent proposition; an AT_LEAST_K expression is accepted only when every permitted K-combination suffices or an explicitly reviewed combinatorial sufficiency contract covers it. A branch that weakens proof strength is rejected at Stage 06.

Every release-bearing evidence path is EVIDENCE_RECORD → OBSERVATION_RECORD → proposition or proof leaf. An observation identifies exact subject, location or measurement point, finding, method/tool, inputs and outputs, hashes, origin, submitting actor, epistemic basis, time/freshness fields, source evidence, scope, and raw-response or native-execution provenance.

Every observation has an accepted relation ESTABLISHES, REFUTES, SUPPORTS_ONLY, CONTEXT_ONLY, DOES_NOT_ADDRESS, or UNKNOWN. Only ESTABLISHES provides affirmative proof; REFUTES provides failure evidence; SUPPORTS_ONLY and CONTEXT_ONLY cannot independently satisfy a proof obligation. Normalization never elevates an external claim.

Absent such a registered contract, the basis remains EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED or weaker.

Semantic sameness is established only by an independent EQUIVALENT review; wording, embeddings, filenames, and hashes cannot merge propositions.
